438	> \(d\) a summary of all change controls implemented during the review period that relate to the Product, the manufacturing process, equipment, or the Facility;
439	>
440	> \(e\) a review of stability data obtained during the review period, including any out-of-trend or out-of-specification results;
441	>
442	> \(f\) a summary of complaints (if any) related to the Product that were received and investigated during the review period;
443	>
444	> \(g\) a summary of the results of any regulatory inspections or Ceritas audits that occurred during the review period;
445	>
446	> \(h\) an assessment of the overall quality performance of the Product and identification of any areas for continuous improvement; and
447	>
448	> \(i\) such other topics as may be required by applicable cGMP regulations or as mutually agreed by the Parties.
449	
450	**8.2 Review and Finalization.**
451	
452	Ceritas shall review the draft APQR provided by Pinnacle and shall provide written comments, questions, or requests for additional information within a reasonable period following receipt. Pinnacle shall address Ceritas\'s comments and incorporate any agreed revisions into the final APQR.
453	
454	The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to finalize the APQR in a timely manner and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. The final APQR shall be approved and signed by the designated quality representatives of both Parties. A copy of the finalized APQR shall be retained by each Party in accordance with the records retention obligations set forth in Section 12.3.
455	
456	**[SECTION 9 --- AUDITS AND REGULATORY INSPECTIONS]{.underline}**
457	
458	**9.1 Ceritas Audit Rights.**
459	
460	Ceritas shall have the right to conduct one (1) GMP audit of the Facility per calendar year, upon twenty (20) business days\' prior written notice to Pinnacle. The scope of any such audit shall be limited to those areas of the Facility and those records that relate directly to the manufacture, testing, packaging, labeling, storage, release, and shipment of the Product and to the performance of Pinnacle\'s obligations under this Quality Agreement. Pinnacle shall provide reasonable access to the Facility, qualified personnel, and relevant documentation during the audit.
461	
462	In addition to the annual routine audit described above, Ceritas may conduct additional audits on a \"for cause\" basis in response to specific events, including but not limited to the occurrence of a Critical Deviation, a product recall, a significant regulatory action (such as the issuance of a Warning Letter or Import Alert), or other circumstances that, in Ceritas\'s reasonable judgment, warrant an audit of the Facility. Any \"for cause\" audit shall be conducted with the mutual agreement of the Parties regarding timing, scope, and logistics. Pinnacle shall use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate Ceritas\'s requests for \"for cause\" audits in a timely manner.
463	
464	Each audit shall be conducted by personnel designated by Ceritas who are qualified to conduct GMP audits. Ceritas\'s audit team may include Ceritas employees, consultants, or third-party auditors retained by Ceritas, provided that any such consultants or third-party auditors have executed confidentiality agreements reasonably acceptable to Pinnacle.
465	
466	**9.2 Audit Reports.**
467	
468	Following the completion of any audit conducted pursuant to Section 9.1, Ceritas shall prepare a written audit report summarizing the findings, observations, and any recommendations arising from the audit. Ceritas shall provide the audit report to Pinnacle within thirty (30) business days of the completion of the audit.
469	
470	Pinnacle shall review the audit report and shall respond to any audit findings or observations within a timeframe mutually agreed upon by the Parties. Pinnacle\'s response shall include, as applicable, an assessment of each finding, identification of the root cause (for significant findings), proposed corrective and preventive actions, and target completion dates for remediation. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to resolve any open audit findings in a timely manner.
471	
472	**9.3 Regulatory Inspections.**
473	
474	Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within five (5) business days of receiving notice of, or becoming aware of, any regulatory inspection by a Regulatory Authority involving the Facility that relates to or may affect the Product. Such notification shall include the identity of the inspecting Regulatory Authority, the scheduled dates of the inspection (if known), and the announced or anticipated scope of the inspection.
475	
476	Following the completion of any such regulatory inspection, Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas, upon request, with copies of any inspection observations issued by the Regulatory Authority (e.g., FDA Form 483 observations, EU GMP non-compliance statements, or equivalent documents) and copies of Pinnacle\'s written responses to such observations. Pinnacle shall provide such copies within a reasonable timeframe following receipt of Ceritas\'s request.
477	
478	The Parties acknowledge that Pinnacle is not obligated under this Quality Agreement to permit Ceritas to participate in, observe, or receive real-time updates during any regulatory inspection. Ceritas acknowledges that the conduct and management of regulatory inspections of the Facility is the responsibility of Pinnacle, and that the presence or participation of Ceritas personnel during such inspections is at the sole discretion of Pinnacle and the inspecting Regulatory Authority.
479	
480	**[SECTION 10 --- PRODUCT RECALL AND FIELD ALERTS]{.underline}**
481	
482	**10.1 Recall Decision-Making.**
483	
484	Decisions regarding the initiation, scope, and conduct of product recalls and field alerts relating to the Product shall be made jointly by the Parties, through consultation and agreement between their respective quality and regulatory affairs functions. Neither Party shall initiate a product recall or issue a field alert with respect to the Product without the prior written consent of the other Party, except where such action is required by a Regulatory Authority. In the event that a Regulatory Authority directs or orders a recall or field alert, the Party receiving such directive shall promptly notify the other Party and the Parties shall cooperate fully in complying with the Regulatory Authority\'s requirements.
485	
486	Each Party shall promptly notify the other Party of any information or event that may give rise to the need for a product recall or field alert, including but not limited to the receipt of adverse event reports, product quality complaints, regulatory communications, or other information suggesting that the Product may not conform to its Specifications or may present a risk to patient safety.
487	
488	**10.2 Cost Allocation.**
489	
490	Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the costs and expenses associated with any product recall or field alert relating to the Product (including direct costs of notification, retrieval, destruction, replacement, and any associated regulatory costs) shall be allocated as follows:
491	
492	> \(a\) In the event that the recall or field alert does not result from the willful misconduct of either Party, the costs shall be shared equally, with each Party bearing fifty percent (50%) of the total costs.
493	>
494	> \(b\) In the event that the recall or field alert results from the willful misconduct of one Party, the Party responsible for the willful misconduct shall bear one hundred percent (100%) of the total costs associated with the recall or field alert.
495	
496	For the avoidance of doubt, the allocation of costs under this Section 10.2 is without prejudice to any indemnification rights or obligations of the Parties under the MSA, and the Parties reserve all rights and remedies available to them under the MSA and applicable law with respect to liability for product recalls and field alerts.
497	
498	**10.3 Cooperation.**
499	
500	Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other Party in the planning, coordination, and execution of any product recall or field alert. Such cooperation shall include, without limitation:
501	
502	> \(a\) providing all information, data, and documentation reasonably requested by the other Party or by any Regulatory Authority in connection with the recall or field alert;
503	>
504	> \(b\) making personnel available for consultation, meetings, and communications with Regulatory Authorities;
505	>
506	> \(c\) assisting with the identification and tracing of affected Batches, distribution channels, and inventory; and
507	>
508	> \(d\) taking such other actions as may be reasonably necessary to protect patient safety and to comply with applicable regulatory requirements.
509	
510	**[SECTION 11 --- SUBCONTRACTING]{.underline}**
511	
512	**11.1 Pre-Approved Subcontractors.**
513	
514	Pinnacle may subcontract analytical testing activities to the pre-approved laboratories listed in Annex C of this Quality Agreement without further consent from or prior notification to Ceritas. The pre-approved laboratories are:
515	
516	> \(a\) Rheintal Analytik AG (Switzerland);
517	>
518	> \(b\) Solara Testing Services Ltd. (United Kingdom); and
519	>
520	> \(c\) QCBio Laboratories, Inc. (Maryland, United States).
521	
522	Pinnacle shall ensure that each pre-approved subcontractor laboratory is and remains qualified to perform the testing activities delegated to it, including compliance with applicable cGMP requirements, applicable regulatory registrations, and Pinnacle\'s quality standards. Pinnacle shall maintain quality agreements or equivalent quality oversight arrangements with each pre-approved subcontractor and shall make such agreements available for review by Ceritas during audits conducted pursuant to Section 9.
523	
524	**11.2 New Subcontractors.**
525	
526	In the event that Pinnacle proposes to engage a subcontractor for testing or other cGMP activities that is not listed in Annex C, Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within fifteen (15) business days of such engagement. The notification shall include the identity and location of the new subcontractor, a description of the scope of activities to be subcontracted, and confirmation that Pinnacle has evaluated and qualified the subcontractor in accordance with Pinnacle\'s supplier qualification procedures.
527	
528	Pinnacle shall be solely responsible for the qualification, oversight, and monitoring of all subcontractors engaged under this Section 11.2, including ensuring that each new subcontractor complies with applicable cGMP requirements and Pinnacle\'s quality standards. The engagement of a new subcontractor does not require the prior written approval of Ceritas, and Ceritas shall not have the right to conduct a qualification audit of a new subcontractor as a condition to such engagement.
529	
530	Ceritas may, however, request that Annex C be updated to reflect any new subcontractor that has been engaged by Pinnacle, and the Parties shall cooperate to update Annex C by written amendment to this Quality Agreement.
531	
532	**11.3 Pinnacle Remains Responsible.**
533	
534	Notwithstanding any subcontracting arrangement, Pinnacle shall remain fully responsible to Ceritas for the quality, accuracy, and compliance of all work performed by any subcontractor in connection with the Product. The subcontracting of any activity shall not relieve Pinnacle of any of its obligations under this Quality Agreement or the MSA. Pinnacle shall be solely responsible for the selection, qualification, monitoring, and oversight of all subcontractors and shall ensure that subcontractor performance meets the requirements of this Quality Agreement and applicable cGMP requirements.
535	
536	**[SECTION 12 --- DATA INTEGRITY AND RECORDS]{.underline}**
537	
538	**12.1 Data Integrity.**
539	
540	Pinnacle shall maintain all electronic records and electronic signatures used in connection with the manufacture, testing, packaging, labeling, storage, and release of the Product in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures), as applicable. Pinnacle\'s compliance program shall address the requirements of 21 CFR Part 11 with respect to system validation, audit trails, system access controls, authority checks, record copying and retention, and electronic signature controls.
541	
542	Pinnacle shall implement and maintain appropriate controls to ensure the integrity, accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability of all data and records generated in connection with the manufacture and testing of the Product, including both electronic and paper-based records. All original data entries shall be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, and accurate (\"ALCOA\"), in accordance with applicable cGMP principles.
543	
544	**12.2 Documentation.**
545	
546	Pinnacle shall maintain all manufacturing, testing, packaging, labeling, and quality records related to the Product in accordance with cGMP requirements and Pinnacle\'s internal document management standard operating procedures. Such records shall include, without limitation, batch production records, batch packaging records, laboratory records and raw data, equipment calibration and qualification records, environmental monitoring records, deviation and CAPA records, change-control records, training records, and validation records.
547	
548	All documentation shall be prepared, reviewed, and approved in accordance with Pinnacle\'s document management SOPs, and shall be maintained in a manner that ensures document security, traceability, and retrieval capability throughout the required retention period.
549	
550	**12.3 Records Retention.**
551	
552	GMP Records related to the Product shall be retained by Pinnacle for the longer of:
553	
554	> \(a\) seven (7) years from the date of Batch release; or
555	>
556	> \(b\) the period required by applicable law, regulation, or regulatory guidance.
557	
558	Upon the expiration of the applicable retention period, Pinnacle may destroy GMP Records in accordance with its internal records management procedures, provided that Pinnacle has given Ceritas at least sixty (60) days\' prior written notice and an opportunity to request transfer or copies of any records scheduled for destruction. Ceritas shall bear the cost of any such transfer or copying.
559	
560	During the retention period, Pinnacle shall maintain the records in a manner that permits timely retrieval and review, and shall make such records available to Ceritas upon reasonable request and during audits conducted pursuant to Section 9.
561	
562	**[SECTION 13 --- STABILITY PROGRAM]{.underline}**
563	
564	**13.1 Scope.**
565	
566	Pinnacle shall perform ongoing stability testing on the Product as part of the commercial stability program, in accordance with applicable cGMP requirements, ICH Q1A (Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products), and the terms of the relevant NDA and EU Marketing Authorisation. The stability program shall encompass both the 25 mg and 100 mg strengths of Velorantib Tablets and shall be designed to confirm that the Product remains within its approved shelf-life Specifications throughout its designated storage period and through expiry.
567	
568	Stability samples shall be stored under the conditions and at the intervals specified in the applicable stability protocols. Pinnacle shall maintain the stability storage chambers used for the Product in a qualified and calibrated state, with continuous temperature and humidity monitoring.
569	
570	**13.2 Protocols and Reporting.**
571	
572	All stability testing shall be performed in accordance with stability protocols mutually agreed upon by the Parties. The Parties shall cooperate to develop and approve stability protocols that are consistent with the commitments made in the NDA and EU Marketing Authorisation and that satisfy applicable regulatory requirements.
573	
574	Pinnacle shall report stability results to Ceritas in quarterly summary reports. Each quarterly stability summary shall include, at a minimum, identification of the Batches on stability, the time points tested during the reporting period, the test results obtained, and an indication of any out-of-trend or out-of-specification results observed.
575	
576	In the event that any stability test result falls outside the approved Specifications or exhibits an out-of-trend or out-of-specification finding, Pinnacle shall promptly notify Ceritas and shall initiate an investigation in accordance with Pinnacle\'s out-of-specification investigation procedures and Section 6 of this Quality Agreement.
577	
578	**[SECTION 14 --- LIABILITY AND FORCE MAJEURE]{.underline}**
579	
580	**14.1 Limitation of Liability.**
581	
582	To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Pinnacle\'s aggregate liability arising under or in connection with this Quality Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or any other legal theory, shall not exceed two million euros (€2,000,000) per calendar year.
583	
584	In no event shall either Party be liable to the other Party for any consequential, indirect, incidental, special, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with this Quality Agreement, regardless of whether such damages were foreseeable or whether either Party has been advised of the possibility of such damages. This exclusion shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and shall include, without limitation, damages for lost profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, and cost of procurement of substitute goods or services.
585	
586	**14.2 Indemnification.**
587	
588	The indemnification rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses arising out of or in connection with the manufacture, testing, packaging, storage, release, and distribution of the Product are set forth in Article 10 of the MSA, which provisions are incorporated herein by reference. To the extent that any indemnification claim relates to quality or cGMP matters governed by this Quality Agreement, the applicable provisions of this Quality Agreement shall be taken into account in determining the parties\' respective responsibilities.
589	
590	**14.3 Force Majeure.**
591	
592	Pinnacle shall be relieved of its obligations under this Quality Agreement to the extent that performance is prevented, delayed, or hindered by a Force Majeure Event, as defined in the MSA. During the continuance of a Force Majeure Event, Pinnacle\'s obligations under this Quality Agreement that are directly affected by the Force Majeure Event shall be suspended, and Pinnacle shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performance resulting from such event.
593	
594	Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing promptly upon the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event that affects or is expected to affect Pinnacle\'s ability to perform its obligations under this Quality Agreement, including a description of the event, the anticipated duration, and the obligations affected. Pinnacle shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact of the Force Majeure Event on its performance and to resume full performance of its obligations as promptly as practicable following the cessation of the Force Majeure Event.
595	
596	**[SECTION 15 --- TERM, TERMINATION, AND SURVIVAL]{.underline}**
597	
598	**15.1 Term.**
599	
600	This Quality Agreement shall become effective as of the date on which it is executed by both Parties (the \"Effective Date\") and shall remain in effect for an initial term of five (5) years from the Effective Date (the \"Initial Term\"). Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Quality Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of two (2) years each (each a \"Renewal Term\"), unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least six (6) months prior to the expiration of the then-current term (whether the Initial Term or any Renewal Term). The Initial Term and all Renewal Terms shall be collectively referred to as the \"Term.\"
601	
602	The Parties acknowledge that the Term of this Quality Agreement is independent of, and not expressly coterminous with, the term of the MSA. In the event that the MSA is terminated or expires prior to the expiration of this Quality Agreement, the Parties shall consult in good faith to determine the appropriate course of action with respect to this Quality Agreement, including whether to terminate, amend, or continue this Quality Agreement.
603	
604	**15.2 Termination.**
605	
606	Either Party may terminate this Quality Agreement in the event of a material breach of this Quality Agreement by the other Party, provided that the terminating Party has given written notice of the breach to the breaching Party and the breaching Party has failed to cure such breach within sixty (60) calendar days following receipt of such written notice. The written notice of breach shall identify the specific provisions of this Quality Agreement that have been breached and shall describe the nature of the breach in reasonable detail.
607	
608	**15.3 Survival.**
609	
610	Upon the expiration or termination of this Quality Agreement for any reason, the following provisions shall survive and continue in full force and effect:
611	
612	> \(a\) The records retention obligations set forth in Section 12.3 shall survive for a period of five (5) years following the date of expiration or termination.
613	>
614	> \(b\) The definitions set forth in Section 2 shall survive to the extent necessary to interpret the surviving provisions.
615	>
616	> \(c\) The provisions of Section 14 (Liability and Force Majeure), Section 16.1 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution), and Section 16.4 (Severability) shall survive indefinitely.
617	
618	All other obligations of the Parties under this Quality Agreement shall cease upon expiration or termination, subject to the completion of any Batch that is in process at the time of expiration or termination, which shall be completed, tested, released, and shipped in accordance with this Quality Agreement and the MSA.
619	
620	**[SECTION 16 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

622	**16.1 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution.**
623	
624	This Quality Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, without regard to its conflict-of-law principles.
625	
626	Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Quality Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, that cannot be resolved by good-faith negotiation between the Parties, shall be finally settled by binding arbitration under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce (\"ICC\"). The arbitration shall be conducted by a tribunal of three (3) arbitrators appointed in accordance with the ICC Rules. The seat of arbitration shall be Frankfurt am Main, Germany. The language of the arbitration shall be English. The arbitral award shall be final and binding on the Parties and may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction.
627	
628	Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction to protect its rights under this Quality Agreement, including but not limited to the protection of confidential information.
629	
630	**16.2 Amendments.**
631	
632	No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Quality Agreement shall be valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, amendments to the Annexes of this Quality Agreement (including updates to Annex A, Annex B, and Annex C) shall require written agreement of both Parties, except as otherwise expressly provided herein.
633	
634	**16.3 Notices.**
635	
636	All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Quality Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered personally, when sent by internationally recognized overnight courier service (with tracking confirmation), or when sent by email (with confirmation of receipt), addressed to the quality contacts and legal contacts set forth in Annex A, or to such other addresses as a Party may designate by written notice to the other Party.
637	
638	**16.4 Severability.**
639	
640	If any provision of this Quality Agreement, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court or arbitral tribunal of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Quality Agreement or the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances. The remaining provisions of this Quality Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, and the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the original intent of the Parties.
641	
642	**16.5 Counterparts.**
643	
644	This Quality Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by email (in PDF format) or other electronic transmission shall be equally as effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
645	
646	**16.6 Entire Agreement.**
647	
648	This Quality Agreement, together with the MSA and its Exhibits, constitutes the entire understanding and agreement between the Parties with respect to quality matters relating to the Product and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, negotiations, discussions, representations, warranties, and understandings, whether oral or written, relating to the subject matter hereof. No terms or conditions of any purchase order, acknowledgment, invoice, or other business form shall modify or supplement this Quality Agreement, and any such terms or conditions are expressly rejected.

13	**[1. Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
14	
15	**[1.1 Purpose]{.underline}**
16	
17	This Quality Agreement Negotiation Playbook (the \"Playbook\") establishes Ceritas Therapeutics, Inc.\'s (\"Ceritas\" or the \"Company\") mandatory, preferred, and fallback negotiation positions for each substantive provision in quality agreements with contract development and manufacturing organizations (\"CDMOs\") and contract testing laboratories (\"CTLs\"). The Playbook is designed to ensure that every quality agreement to which Ceritas is a party (a) allocates quality responsibilities in a manner that protects patient safety, product quality, and regulatory compliance, (b) preserves Ceritas\'s ultimate authority as the holder of applicable marketing authorizations and new drug applications, and (c) reflects a consistent, defensible approach to risk allocation that has been vetted by both the Quality Assurance and Legal functions.
18	
19	The Playbook serves as the primary reference document for the cross-functional team responsible for negotiating quality agreements. It is intended to accelerate negotiations by clearly articulating the Company\'s opening positions, the range of acceptable concessions, and the points on which no concession is permitted without executive-level authorization. By defining these parameters in advance, the Playbook reduces cycle times, minimizes the risk of ad hoc decision-making during negotiations, and creates a documented audit trail of the Company\'s quality-risk-management reasoning.
20	
21	**[1.2 Scope]{.underline}**
22	
23	This Playbook applies to all quality agreements entered into, renewed, or materially amended by Ceritas for commercial products and late-stage clinical products (Phase 2b and later). It has particular applicability to quality agreements covering Tier 1 --- Critical Revenue Products, which currently include Velorantib (NDA 215-847; EU Marketing Authorisation held by Ceritas Therapeutics Ireland DAC) and any other product designated as Tier 1 by the Senior Vice President, Quality & Regulatory.
24	
25	The Playbook covers quality agreements with all categories of external manufacturing and testing partners, including but not limited to:
26	
27	> • Drug substance CDMOs
28	>
29	> • Drug product CDMOs (including fill-finish operations)
30	>
31	> • Primary and secondary packaging CDMOs
32	>
33	> • Analytical testing laboratories (release and stability)
34	>
35	> • Microbiological testing laboratories
36	>
37	> • Raw-material and excipient suppliers where a quality agreement is required
38	
39	Early-phase clinical programs (Phase 1 through Phase 2a) may apply this Playbook at the discretion of the lead quality reviewer but are not required to do so unless the program involves a product that has been designated as strategically critical by the Chief Medical Officer or the Senior Vice President, Quality & Regulatory.
40	
41	**[1.3 Relationship to Master Services Agreements]{.underline}**
42	
43	Quality agreements negotiated under this Playbook operate in conjunction with, but are legally and functionally distinct from, Master Services Agreements (\"MSAs\"), statements of work, and commercial supply agreements entered into between Ceritas and its CDMOs or CTLs. In the event of a conflict between the terms of a Quality Agreement and the terms of an MSA or any commercial agreement, the Quality Agreement shall prevail with respect to all matters relating to product quality, regulatory compliance, and GMP obligations.
44	
45	Every Quality Agreement must be consistent with the requirements of ICH Q10 (*Pharmaceutical Quality System*), 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 (Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals), EU GMP Annex 16 (*Certification by a Qualified Person and Batch Release*), and any other applicable regulatory standards. This Playbook governs the internal review standard against which any counterparty-drafted quality agreement is evaluated prior to execution. Where a counterparty draft is silent on an issue addressed in this Playbook, the absence constitutes a gap that must be raised during the review process.
46	
47	**[1.4 Defined Position Hierarchy]{.underline}**
48	
49	The Playbook establishes three tiers of negotiation positions for each substantive provision:
50	
51	**Mandatory Position.** A Mandatory Position represents a non-negotiable requirement. Ceritas\'s negotiators are not authorized to concede, waive, or modify a Mandatory Position under any circumstances without a joint written exception signed by the Vice President, Quality Assurance and the Associate General Counsel, Commercial Transactions. Any concession of a Mandatory Position must be documented in the negotiation file with a written risk assessment explaining the basis for the exception, the residual risk to product quality, and any compensating controls that will be implemented.
52	
53	**Preferred Position.** A Preferred Position represents the desired contractual outcome that the negotiation team should seek to achieve. A Preferred Position may be conceded to the corresponding Fallback Position with documented justification from the lead quality reviewer. The documented justification must identify the specific counterparty concern or business rationale that supports the concession and must confirm that the resulting contractual language still meets the Mandatory Position for the provision in question.
54	
55	**Fallback Position.** A Fallback Position represents the minimum acceptable position for a given provision. Concession below a Fallback Position is prohibited absent executive-level exception --- specifically, written approval from a Senior Vice President or above, supported by a documented risk assessment prepared jointly by Quality Assurance and Legal. Any such exception must be tracked in the Quality Agreement Negotiation Log maintained by the Playbook Owner.
56	
57	Where a provision is identified as having only a Mandatory Position (i.e., no Preferred or Fallback tiers are listed), the Mandatory Position is the sole acceptable outcome and there is no permissible concession.
58	
59	**[2. Roles and Responsibilities for Playbook Application]{.underline}**
60	
61	**[2.1 Playbook Owner]{.underline}**
62	
63	The Playbook Owner is **Dr. Mariel Castaño-Webb, Vice President, Quality Assurance**. The Playbook Owner is responsible for maintaining the currency and accuracy of this Playbook, approving revisions, resolving interpretive questions regarding the application of negotiation positions, and serving as the senior Quality Assurance decision-maker for exception requests related to Mandatory and Fallback Positions.
64	
65	The Playbook Owner may delegate day-to-day coordination of Playbook application to a designee within the Quality Assurance function, provided that such delegation is documented in writing and the Playbook Owner retains final authority over all exception decisions requiring VP Quality approval.
66	
67	**[2.2 Legal Reviewer]{.underline}**
68	
69	The Legal Reviewer is **Jonathan R. Hadley, Associate General Counsel, Commercial Transactions**. The Legal Reviewer is responsible for ensuring that all quality agreement language is legally enforceable, consistent with the Company\'s standard contracting practices, and aligned with the MSA and other commercial agreements governing the relevant CDMO or CTL relationship. The Legal Reviewer co-signs all exception requests for Mandatory Position concessions and provides legal risk assessments as part of the escalation process described in Section 20.
70	
71	The Legal Reviewer coordinates with outside counsel as needed on jurisdiction-specific issues, including compliance with EU GMP requirements, cross-border data-transfer restrictions, and foreign-law considerations that may arise when negotiating with CDMOs located outside the United States.
72	
73	**[2.3 Review Process]{.underline}**
74	
75	All counterparty-drafted quality agreements and quality agreement amendments must be reviewed against this Playbook on a section-by-section basis before any redline, markup, or counterproposal is returned to the counterparty. The review process is as follows:
76	
77	1\. **Receipt and Logging.** Upon receipt of a counterparty draft, the lead quality reviewer logs the document in the Quality Agreement Negotiation Log, assigns a tracking number, and distributes copies to the cross-functional review team (Quality Assurance, Legal, Regulatory Affairs, and Supply Chain, as applicable).
78	
79	2\. **Section-by-Section Assessment.** The lead quality reviewer prepares a written assessment comparing each substantive section of the counterparty draft against the corresponding Playbook provisions. The assessment identifies, for each provision: (a) whether the counterparty language meets, exceeds, or falls short of the Mandatory Position; (b) any gaps or omissions relative to the Playbook; and (c) recommended redline language.
80	
81	3\. **Issues/Risk Memorandum.** Any deviations from the Playbook --- whether proposed by the counterparty or recommended by a member of the cross-functional team --- are documented in an Issues/Risk Memorandum. The memorandum identifies the specific Playbook provision at issue, describes the deviation, assesses the quality and business risk associated with the deviation, and recommends a negotiation strategy (e.g., insist on Mandatory Position, concede to Preferred Position, escalate for exception).
82	
83	4\. **Cross-Functional Alignment.** The cross-functional team meets (in person or by videoconference) to review the Issues/Risk Memorandum and agree on a unified redline. Unresolved issues are escalated to the Playbook Owner and the Legal Reviewer for resolution.
84	
85	5\. **Redline Return.** The unified redline is returned to the counterparty by the lead quality reviewer or the Legal Reviewer, as appropriate. The Issues/Risk Memorandum is retained in the negotiation file and is not shared with the counterparty.
86	
87	6\. **Final Execution.** Before execution, the final quality agreement is re-reviewed against the Playbook to confirm that all Mandatory Positions are satisfied and that any concessions have been properly documented and approved.
88	
89	**[3. General Drafting Principles]{.underline}**
90	
91	**[3.1 Identification of Ceritas as NDA Holder / MAH]{.underline}**
92	
93	Ceritas must be identified throughout the Quality Agreement as the NDA holder (for the United States) or the Marketing Authorisation Holder (\"MAH\") (for the European Union and other jurisdictions, as applicable). The Quality Agreement must explicitly state that Ceritas retains ultimate quality oversight authority over all activities performed by the CDMO or CTL under the agreement. Language that characterizes the parties\' relationship as a \"partnership,\" \"joint venture,\" or other arrangement implying shared or co-equal quality authority is unacceptable. The CDMO or CTL acts as a service provider performing delegated activities under Ceritas\'s oversight, and the Quality Agreement must reflect this dynamic unambiguously.
94	
95	Where the EU Marketing Authorisation is held by Ceritas Therapeutics Ireland DAC (a wholly-owned subsidiary), the Quality Agreement must identify both Ceritas Therapeutics, Inc. and Ceritas Therapeutics Ireland DAC as applicable and delineate the respective roles of each entity. Under no circumstances may the Quality Agreement omit identification of the MAH for EU markets or delegate final quality authority for EU-market product to the CDMO without appropriate limitations as described in Section 6 of this Playbook.
96	
97	**[3.2 Specificity of Obligations]{.underline}**
98	
99	All GMP and regulatory obligations set forth in the Quality Agreement must be stated with specificity. The use of \"commercially reasonable efforts,\" \"best efforts,\" \"reasonable endeavors,\" or similar qualified-obligation language is prohibited for any provision that relates to compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practice (\"cGMP\"), regulatory reporting obligations, product specifications, or patient-safety requirements. These qualifiers introduce subjective standards that are incompatible with the binary nature of GMP compliance and create enforcement ambiguity that is unacceptable from both a regulatory and a quality-risk-management perspective.
100	
101	Where a timeline is specified (e.g., notification deadlines, investigation timelines, reporting periods), the obligation must be stated in terms of a fixed number of calendar days or business days, as applicable, without qualifiers such as \"as soon as practicable\" or \"within a reasonable time.\" If the counterparty proposes qualified language for a timeline obligation, the lead quality reviewer must replace it with a specific numeric deadline consistent with the positions set forth in this Playbook.
102	
103	**[3.3 Required Annexes]{.underline}**
104	
105	Every Quality Agreement governed by this Playbook must include, at a minimum, the following annexes:
106	
107	> • **Annex A --- Contact Lists.** Identification of key quality, regulatory, and operational contacts at both Ceritas and the CDMO/CTL, including names, titles, email addresses, and telephone numbers. The annex must include a designated contact for deviation and complaint notifications and must specify the process for updating contact information.
108	>
109	> • **Annex B --- Specifications.** Complete product specifications for each product manufactured or tested under the Quality Agreement, including in-process controls, release specifications, and shelf-life specifications.
110	>
111	> • **Annex C --- Approved Test Methods.** A list of all validated test methods approved by Ceritas for use in the manufacture, testing, and release of product under the Quality Agreement, with references to the applicable method-validation reports.
112	>
113	> • **Annex D --- Complaint-Handling Procedure.** A detailed complaint-handling procedure meeting the requirements of Section 18 of this Playbook.
114	
115	Additional annexes (e.g., change-control classification matrix, stability protocols, approved subcontractor list) may be included as necessary to support the specific CDMO or CTL relationship. Omission of any of the four required annexes constitutes a critical gap that must be raised with the counterparty during the review process and resolved prior to execution.
116	
117	**[4. Change Control]{.underline}**
118	
119	Effective change control is among the most critical provisions in any quality agreement. Unapproved or inadequately communicated changes by a CDMO represent one of the highest-risk categories for product-quality failures, regulatory observations, and potential patient harm. The positions set forth below are designed to ensure that Ceritas maintains full visibility into and approval authority over all changes that could affect the product.
120	
121	**[4.1 Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
122	
123	The CDMO must obtain **prior written approval** from Ceritas for any change to process, equipment, facility, or raw-material supplier that could affect product identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency. This requirement extends to, but is not limited to, changes to:
124	
125	> • Manufacturing process parameters, process steps, and in-process controls
126	>
127	> • Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packaging, or testing of the product, including like-for-like equipment replacements
128	>
129	> • Facility modifications, including HVAC, water systems, clean-room classifications, and environmental monitoring programs
130	>
131	> • Raw-material and excipient suppliers, including changes to the grade, source, or synthesis route of any raw material or excipient
132	>
133	> • Primary and secondary packaging components and suppliers
134	>
135	> • Testing methods, reference standards, and analytical instruments used for release or stability testing
136	>
137	> • Software systems used to control, monitor, or record GMP activities (including laboratory information management systems and manufacturing execution systems)
138	
139	The minimum advance notice period for any such change is **90 calendar days** before the proposed implementation date. The 90-day period commences upon Ceritas\'s receipt of a complete change-notification package, which must include: (a) a description of the proposed change, (b) the rationale for the change, (c) a risk assessment evaluating the potential impact on product quality and regulatory status, (d) proposed qualification and/or validation activities, and (e) a proposed implementation timeline.
140	
141	No change may be implemented without documented Ceritas approval. Provisions that characterize Ceritas\'s role as limited to \"notify and comment\" --- i.e., requiring only that Ceritas be notified of the change with an opportunity to provide non-binding comments --- are unacceptable. Similarly, \"commercially reasonable efforts to notify\" or \"commercially reasonable efforts to obtain approval\" formulations are unacceptable because they introduce a subjective qualifier into a binary compliance obligation.
142	
143	**[4.2 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
144	
145	In addition to the Mandatory Position, the Preferred Position includes the following elements:
146	
147	A **change classification matrix** shall be appended to the Quality Agreement as an annex. The matrix shall categorize potential changes as Critical, Major, or Minor based on their assessed impact on product quality and regulatory compliance. The classification criteria and examples shall be specified in the annex with sufficient detail to minimize ambiguity. Ceritas retains sole authority to classify any change within the matrix; in the event of a disagreement between Ceritas and the CDMO regarding the classification of a proposed change, Ceritas\'s classification shall prevail.
148	
149	For emergency safety-related changes --- defined as changes necessary to address an immediate threat to patient safety, product quality, or facility safety that cannot reasonably wait for the standard prior-approval process --- the CDMO may implement the change with concurrent notice to Ceritas. Concurrent notice must be provided by email to the designated Ceritas quality contact within four (4) hours of implementation of the emergency change, followed by a formal written change notification within twenty-four (24) hours. Formal written Ceritas approval of the emergency change must be obtained within five (5) business days of the implementation date. If Ceritas does not approve the emergency change, the CDMO must promptly reverse the change or implement an alternative approved by Ceritas, unless reversal would itself create a safety risk, in which case the parties shall confer immediately to agree on a corrective course of action.
150	
151	**[4.3 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
152	
153	The advance notice period may be reduced from 90 calendar days to **60 calendar days**, but only with the written exception of the VP Quality (Dr. Mariel Castaño-Webb), documented in the negotiation file. The exception memorandum must explain why the counterparty\'s insistence on a shorter notice period is commercially justified and must identify any compensating controls (e.g., enhanced Ceritas oversight of the CDMO\'s internal change-control process, periodic review of the CDMO\'s change-control log) that will mitigate the risk associated with the shortened timeline.
154	
155	Even at the Fallback Position, the requirement for prior written approval from Ceritas before implementation of any change remains **non-negotiable**. There is no Fallback Position that permits \"notify and comment\" or any other formulation that falls short of prior written approval.
156	
157	**[5. Deviation and CAPA Management]{.underline}**
158	
159	Deviations and corrective and preventive actions (\"CAPAs\") are fundamental elements of the pharmaceutical quality system. The ability of Ceritas, as the NDA holder and MAH, to monitor, evaluate, and approve the resolution of deviations at contract sites is essential to maintaining control over product quality and meeting regulatory expectations. The following positions establish Ceritas\'s requirements for deviation notification, root-cause analysis, and CAPA authority.
160	
161	**[5.1 Deviation Notification --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
162	
163	The CDMO must notify Ceritas of all deviations related to the product, the manufacturing process, the facility, or any quality system element that could affect the product, in accordance with the following timelines:
164	
165	> • **Critical Deviations:** The CDMO must notify Ceritas within **24 hours** of detection of the deviation. A critical deviation is one that has resulted in, or has the potential to result in, a product that does not conform to its approved specifications, that poses a risk to patient safety, or that may require a field alert or recall.
166	>
167	> • **Major Deviations:** The CDMO must notify Ceritas within **5 business days** of detection of the deviation. A major deviation is one that represents a significant departure from approved procedures, specifications, or validated processes but that does not, based on the initial assessment, pose an immediate risk to product quality or patient safety.
168	>
169	> • **Minor Deviations:** The CDMO must notify Ceritas within **5 business days** of detection of the deviation. A minor deviation is one that represents a limited departure from approved procedures that does not affect product quality, safety, or efficacy.
170	
171	In all cases, notification must be in writing. Email notification to the designated Ceritas quality contact is acceptable for initial notice of critical and major deviations, provided that a formal written deviation report follows within the timeline specified for root-cause analysis (see Section 5.2).
172	
173	Monthly summary reporting of deviations is acceptable as a supplemental reporting mechanism but is **not acceptable** as the sole or primary means of notification for critical or major deviations. Any Quality Agreement provision that limits CDMO notification obligations to periodic summary reports is unacceptable and must be revised to include the event-driven notification timelines specified above.
174	
175	**[5.2 Root-Cause Analysis Timelines --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
176	
177	The CDMO must complete a root-cause analysis and submit the analysis to Ceritas in accordance with the following timelines:
178	
179	> • **Critical Deviations:** Root-cause analysis completed and submitted to Ceritas within **15 business days** of deviation detection.
180	>
181	> • **Major Deviations:** Root-cause analysis completed and submitted to Ceritas within **30 business days** of deviation detection.
182	
183	These timelines represent maximum periods, and earlier submission is expected wherever feasible. Extensions to these timelines are permitted only with **prior written approval** from Ceritas QA. Extension requests must include: (a) an explanation of the reason the timeline cannot be met, (b) a summary of work completed to date, (c) a proposed revised completion date, and (d) any interim risk-mitigation measures that have been implemented.
184	
185	Root-cause analysis must be conducted using a structured methodology (e.g., Ishikawa diagram, 5 Whys, fault-tree analysis) and must be supported by objective data. Conclusory statements of root cause without supporting evidence are not acceptable.
186	
187	**[5.3 CAPA Authority --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
188	
189	Ceritas retains **sole authority** to approve or reject CAPA plans for critical deviations. The CDMO must submit a proposed CAPA plan to Ceritas for review and written approval before any corrective or preventive action is implemented in response to a critical deviation. The CDMO may not implement a CAPA plan for a critical deviation unless and until Ceritas has provided written approval.
190	
191	Language that limits Ceritas\'s role to \"input,\" \"consultation,\" or \"review and comment\" with respect to CAPA plans for critical deviations is insufficient and unacceptable. Ceritas\'s approval must be stated as a condition precedent to CAPA implementation for all critical deviations.
192	
193	**[5.4 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
194	
195	The Preferred Position extends Ceritas\'s approval authority to CAPA plans for **major deviations** in addition to critical deviations. Under the Preferred Position, the CDMO must submit proposed CAPA plans for both critical and major deviations to Ceritas for written approval prior to implementation.
196	
197	In addition, CAPA effectiveness checks must be performed by the CDMO at defined intervals following CAPA implementation and reported to Ceritas with supporting data demonstrating the effectiveness (or lack thereof) of the implemented corrective and preventive actions. The frequency and criteria for effectiveness checks shall be specified in the approved CAPA plan.
198	
199	**[5.5 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
200	
201	At the Fallback Position, Ceritas\'s **approval authority for critical deviation CAPAs remains non-negotiable** and may not be conceded under any circumstances.
202	
203	For major deviations, the Fallback Position permits the CDMO to retain implementation authority for CAPA plans, provided that Ceritas retains the right to **review and comment** on proposed CAPA plans prior to implementation and the CDMO has an affirmative obligation to address Ceritas\'s comments **in good faith** before implementing the CAPA. \"Good faith\" requires the CDMO to engage substantively with each Ceritas comment and either incorporate the comment or provide a documented, scientifically justified rationale for declining to do so. Mere acknowledgment of Ceritas\'s comments without substantive engagement does not satisfy the good-faith obligation.
204	
205	**[6. Batch Release and Certificate of Analysis]{.underline}**
206	
207	Batch release is the point at which the CDMO\'s manufacturing and quality operations converge with Ceritas\'s regulatory obligations as the NDA holder and MAH. The allocation of disposition authority and the quality of batch-release documentation are critical to ensuring that only product meeting approved specifications reaches patients. The following positions govern the negotiation of batch-release and Certificate of Analysis provisions.
208	
209	**[6.1 Disposition Authority --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
210	
211	Ceritas QP/QA retains **final batch disposition authority** for all markets, including both the United States (under NDA 215-847) and the European Union (under the Marketing Authorisation held by Ceritas Therapeutics Ireland DAC).
212	
213	Any Quality Agreement provision that grants the CDMO\'s Qualified Person (\"QP\") final and unrestricted disposition authority for any market is unacceptable without express Ceritas QA approval. Where EU GMP Annex 16 requires QP certification by a QP employed by or contracted to the manufacturer, the Quality Agreement must limit the CDMO QP\'s authority to the specific act of EU QP certification required under Annex 16, and Ceritas must retain the overriding right to reject any batch notwithstanding the CDMO QP\'s certification. In practice, this means that:
214	
215	> • The CDMO QP performs the certification required by EU GMP Annex 16 for EU market release.
216	>
217	> • Ceritas QA independently reviews batch documentation and release-testing results and makes a separate, final disposition decision for the United States and all other non-EU markets.
218	>
219	> • Even for EU markets, Ceritas retains the right to direct the CDMO not to release a certified batch if Ceritas determines, in its sole discretion, that the batch does not meet Ceritas\'s quality standards, regardless of the CDMO QP\'s certification.
220	
221	Provisions that characterize the CDMO QP\'s certification as the final and binding disposition decision for all purposes, without preserving Ceritas\'s override authority, are unacceptable.
222	
223	**[6.2 Certificate of Analysis --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
224	
225	A full Certificate of Analysis (\"CoA\") must be provided with each batch shipment. The CoA must include, at a minimum:
226	
227	> • Product name, batch number, and manufacturing date
228	>
229	> • All release-test results, including results for each individual test listed in the approved specifications
230	>
231	> • Specification limits for each test
232	>
233	> • Reference to the validated, Ceritas-approved test methods used for each analysis
234	>
235	> • Statement of batch disposition (approved/rejected)
236	>
237	> • Signature and date of the authorized quality representative
238	
239	The CoA must reference validated, Ceritas-approved test methods. Use of non-approved or modified test methods without prior Ceritas approval is a deviation that must be immediately reported in accordance with Section 5 of this Playbook.
240	
241	**[6.3 Raw Data Access --- Preferred Position]{.underline}**
242	
243	The Preferred Position requires that the CDMO make raw data packages (including chromatograms, spectra, raw instrument data, and complete laboratory notebook entries) available to Ceritas upon request within **2 business days** of the request. This enables Ceritas QA to perform independent verification of release-test results and to support trending, annual product quality reviews, and regulatory submissions.
244	
245	Turnaround times exceeding 2 business days for raw data requests represent a deviation from the Preferred Position and should be noted in the negotiation file.
246	
247	**[6.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
248	
249	At the Fallback Position, the turnaround time for raw data requests shall not exceed **5 business days**. Any period longer than 5 business days is unacceptable and falls below the Fallback Position, requiring executive-level exception. The 5-business-day turnaround must be stated as a firm contractual obligation, not as a \"target\" or \"commercially reasonable\" timeline.
250	
251	**[7. Annual Product Quality Review (APQR)]{.underline}**
252	
253	The Annual Product Quality Review is a cornerstone of the pharmaceutical quality system and a regulatory expectation under ICH Q10 and 21 CFR 211.180(e). The APQR provides a comprehensive assessment of the product\'s quality performance over the preceding year and serves as the basis for identifying trends, evaluating the adequacy of specifications and manufacturing processes, and determining whether any corrective or preventive actions are warranted.
254	
255	**[7.1 Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
256	
257	The CDMO must prepare and submit a draft APQR to Ceritas no later than **60 calendar days** after the close of each calendar year (i.e., by March 1 of each year for the preceding calendar year). The APQR must cover all parameters required by ICH Q10 and 21 CFR 211.180(e), including but not limited to:
258	
259	> • A review of all batches manufactured during the reporting period, including any batches that were rejected or reprocessed
260	>
261	> • A summary of all deviations, investigations, out-of-specification results, and CAPAs
262	>
263	> • A review of critical in-process controls and finished-product results
264	>
265	> • Trending of critical quality attributes and process parameters
266	>
267	> • A summary of all changes to the manufacturing process, specifications, analytical methods, or facilities
268	>
269	> • A review of the stability program and stability data
270	>
271	> • A review of all product-related complaints
272	>
273	> • An assessment of the status and adequacy of post-approval commitments and regulatory submissions
274	>
275	> • A review of qualification and validation activities
276	
277	Ceritas retains the right to review, comment on, and require revisions to the draft APQR before finalization. The CDMO must incorporate Ceritas\'s comments and submit a revised APQR within 15 business days of receipt of Ceritas\'s comments.
278	
279	**[7.2 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
280	
281	The Preferred Position requires that the CDMO submit the draft APQR within **45 calendar days** after the close of each calendar year (i.e., by February 14 of each year). The earlier submission date provides Ceritas with additional time to review the draft, reconcile the APQR data with Ceritas\'s internal quality records, and finalize the report in advance of internal management review deadlines and regulatory submission timelines.
282

284

287	**[8. Audit and Inspection Rights]{.underline}**
288	
289	Audit rights are essential to Ceritas\'s ability to exercise oversight of its contract manufacturing and testing operations and to satisfy the regulatory expectation that the NDA holder and MAH maintain a program of periodic supplier evaluation. The following positions address both routine and for-cause audit rights.
290	
291	**[8.1 Routine Audit Rights --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
292	
293	Ceritas has the right to conduct on-site GMP audits of the CDMO\'s manufacturing, testing, packaging, and storage facilities with **10 business days\'** written notice to the CDMO. The Quality Agreement must not impose any cap on audit frequency; Ceritas is entitled to conduct an unlimited number of audits per calendar year at its discretion, based on risk assessment, product performance, and regulatory requirements.
294	
295	Notice periods exceeding 10 business days are unacceptable. Similarly, frequency limitations --- such as provisions restricting Ceritas to one audit per calendar year, or requiring that audits be limited to \"normal business hours\" without further specification --- are unacceptable. Ceritas expects to conduct audits during the CDMO\'s operating hours, but the Quality Agreement must not impose restrictions that would, in practice, limit Ceritas\'s ability to observe operations as they are actually performed.
296	
297	The CDMO must provide Ceritas\'s audit team with reasonable access to all areas of the facility involved in the manufacture, testing, packaging, or storage of the product, as well as access to all relevant GMP documentation, including batch records, deviation reports, CAPA files, training records, equipment qualification and process validation records, and data-integrity program documentation.
298	
299	**[8.2 For-Cause Audit Rights --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
300	
301	Ceritas may conduct for-cause audits at any time with reasonable notice, which shall be a minimum of **48 hours**. 302	
303	The Quality Agreement must not require mutual agreement as a condition to a for-cause audit. Provisions that require the CDMO to \"agree\" to the audit, to \"confirm availability,\" or to otherwise exercise a de facto veto over Ceritas\'s for-cause audit rights are unacceptable.
304	
305	**[8.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
306	
307	Under the Preferred Position, Ceritas may include third-party auditors, consultants, or subject-matter experts as members of the Ceritas audit team. Third-party auditors engaged by Ceritas must be subject to confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those imposed on Ceritas under the Quality Agreement or the MSA, and Ceritas must ensure that each third-party auditor has executed an appropriate confidentiality agreement before being granted access to the CDMO\'s facility or confidential information.
308	
309	**[8.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
310	
311	At the Fallback Position, routine audit frequency may be set at no fewer than **two (2) on-site GMP audits per calendar year**, with for-cause audits remaining unlimited. 312	
313	Even at the Fallback Position, the notice period for routine audits shall not exceed **10 business days**, and the 48-hour minimum notice for for-cause audits remains unchanged.

317	Regulatory inspections of CDMO facilities represent high-stakes events with potentially significant consequences for Ceritas\'s product approvals, marketing authorizations, and regulatory standing. 322

324	>
325	> • The stated scope of the inspection, if provided by the authority
326	>
327	> • The anticipated dates of the inspection
328	>
329	> • Any other relevant information available to the CDMO at the time of notification

333	**[9.2 Participation and Observation --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**

335	Ceritas has the right to participate in and observe any regulatory inspection that relates to Velorantib or to the manufacturing line, testing laboratory, or facility area used for the manufacture, testing, packaging, or storage of Velorantib. 336	
337	The CDMO must provide Ceritas with copies of all inspection observations (e.g., FDA Form 483 observations, EMA inspection findings), the CDMO\'s responses to inspection observations, and all correspondence with the inspecting authority relating to the inspection, within **2 business days** of issuance or receipt.
338	
339	**[9.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
340	
341	Under the Preferred Position, Ceritas has the right to **review and approve** the CDMO\'s responses to inspection observations before submission to the inspecting authority. Ceritas\'s approval must be obtained before the response is submitted. This reflects the principle that inspection findings at a contract site may have direct consequences for Ceritas\'s regulatory standing and marketing authorizations, and Ceritas must therefore have the opportunity to ensure that responses are accurate, complete, and consistent with Ceritas\'s global regulatory strategy.
342	
343	**[9.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
344	
345	At the Fallback Position, Ceritas has the right to **review and comment on** (but not approve) the CDMO\'s responses to inspection observations before submission to the inspecting authority. 347	**[10. Recall and Field Alert]{.underline}**
348	
349	Product recalls and field alerts are among the most consequential quality events in the pharmaceutical industry, with the potential to affect patient safety, product availability, regulatory relationships, and company reputation. The allocation of recall decision-making authority and cost responsibility must be clearly defined in the Quality Agreement.
350	
351	**[10.1 Decision Authority --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
352	
353	Ceritas has **sole decision-making authority** over product recalls and field alerts (including FDA Field Alert Reports under 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1)). The Quality Agreement must not grant the CDMO \"joint\" decision-making authority, veto rights, or the right to condition its cooperation on agreement with Ceritas\'s recall decision. The CDMO\'s obligation to cooperate with any recall directed by Ceritas must be unconditional and immediate.
354	
355	This allocation of authority is consistent with Ceritas\'s regulatory obligations as the NDA holder and MAH. Under applicable law and regulation, the ultimate responsibility for recall decisions rests with the marketing authorization holder, and the Quality Agreement must reflect this allocation without qualification.
356	
357	**[10.2 Cost Allocation --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
358	
359	The CDMO must bear the costs of any recall to the extent that the recall arises from the CDMO\'s failure to comply with cGMP requirements, the approved product specifications, or the terms of the Quality Agreement. This cost allocation applies regardless of whether the CDMO\'s non-compliance is characterized as negligent, grossly negligent, or willful.
360	
361	Provisions that impose a 50/50 cost-sharing arrangement regardless of fault, or that limit the CDMO\'s cost responsibility to instances of \"willful misconduct\" or \"gross negligence\" only, are unacceptable. Such provisions would effectively shift the financial consequences of CDMO quality failures to Ceritas, creating a misalignment of incentives that is incompatible with sound quality-risk management.
362	
363	**[10.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
364	
365	Under the Preferred Position, the CDMO bears all direct and consequential recall costs attributable to a CDMO root cause. \"Recall costs\" encompass, without limitation:
366	
367	> • Logistics and transportation costs for product retrieval and destruction
368	>
369	> • Customer and distributor notification costs
370	>
371	> • Replacement product manufacturing costs
372	>
373	> • Regulatory agency communications and submission costs
374	>
375	> • Third-party warehousing and quarantine costs
376	>
377	> • Ceritas internal costs reasonably incurred in managing the recall, including dedicated personnel time and external consultant fees
378	
379	**[10.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
380	
381	At the Fallback Position, cost allocation is **proportional to fault** as determined through a documented root-cause investigation. In cases of shared causation, costs are allocated in proportion to each party\'s relative contribution to the root cause. However, even at the Fallback Position, Ceritas retains **sole recall authority** in all cases. The CDMO may not use a cost-allocation dispute as a basis for refusing to cooperate with a Ceritas-directed recall.
382

385	The use of subcontractors by CDMOs introduces additional layers of risk into the supply chain and attenuates Ceritas\'s ability to exercise direct quality oversight. 396

405	**[12. Data Integrity and Records Retention]{.underline}**
406	
407	Data integrity is a foundational element of the pharmaceutical quality system and a subject of heightened regulatory scrutiny from the FDA, EMA, MHRA, and other global regulators. The following positions ensure that CDMOs and CTLs maintain robust data-integrity programs and retain GMP records for periods consistent with Ceritas\'s regulatory and legal requirements.
408	
409	**[12.1 Data Integrity Program --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
410	
411	The CDMO must maintain a comprehensive data-integrity program consistent with the requirements and expectations set forth in the **FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers --- Guidance for Industry (2018)** and the **MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance and Definitions (2018)**. The data-integrity program must address, at a minimum, the following elements:
412	
413	> • **Organizational and Cultural Controls:** Assignment of data-integrity responsibilities, management commitment, training programs, and a culture that encourages reporting of data-integrity issues without retaliation.
414	>
415	> • **Procedural Controls:** Written procedures for data generation, processing, review, and reporting; procedures for the identification, investigation, and resolution of data-integrity incidents; and procedures for audit-trail review.
416	>
417	> • **Technical Controls:** System-level access controls, audit-trail functionality, electronic-signature compliance, data backup and recovery, and validated computer systems used to generate, process, or store GMP data.
418	
419	Compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures) alone is insufficient to satisfy this requirement. Part 11 addresses a specific subset of data-integrity considerations, and Ceritas requires that the CDMO\'s program encompass the broader organizational, procedural, and technical controls described in the FDA and MHRA guidance documents.
420	
421	**[12.2 Records Retention --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
422	
423	All GMP records related to Ceritas product must be maintained by the CDMO for the longer of (a) **10 years** from the date of batch release or (b) the period required by applicable law or regulation. 424	
425	Retention periods shorter than 10 years are unacceptable. Quality Agreement provisions proposing 5-year or 7-year retention periods, or retention \"in accordance with the CDMO\'s standard retention schedule\" without specifying a minimum period, must be revised to meet the 10-year minimum.
426	
427	Upon termination or expiration of the Quality Agreement, all GMP records must be retained for the remainder of the applicable retention period or, at Ceritas\'s election, transferred to Ceritas or a Ceritas designee in a format acceptable to Ceritas.
428	
429	**[12.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
430	
431	Under the Preferred Position, the CDMO provides an **annual self-assessment report** on the maturity and effectiveness of its data-integrity program. The report must be shared with Ceritas QA no later than 60 calendar days after the close of each calendar year and must include, at a minimum: (a) a summary of data-integrity audits and assessments conducted during the year, (b) a summary of data-integrity incidents identified and their resolution, (c) an assessment of the status of any open remediation activities, and (d) management\'s overall assessment of the program\'s maturity level.
432	
433	In addition, all GMP records should be stored in validated electronic systems with full audit-trail functionality, enabling reconstruction of the complete data lifecycle for any GMP record upon request.
434	
435	**[12.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
436	
437	The **10-year minimum retention period is non-negotiable** and may not be conceded under any circumstances. This element is treated as a Mandatory Position even at the Fallback tier.

439	**[13. Stability Program]{.underline}**

441	Ongoing stability testing is a regulatory requirement under ICH Q1A, ICH Q1E, and 21 CFR 211.166, and provides essential data for confirming product shelf life, supporting post-approval changes, and identifying trends that may warrant corrective action. 443	**[13.1 Protocol Approval --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**

This accelerated reporting timeline enables Ceritas to assess the potential impact on marketed product, initiate risk-based investigations, and determine whether regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., annual stability update reports, NDA field alert reports) are triggered.

459	**[13.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**

485	**[15. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**
486	
487	Limitation-of-liability provisions in quality agreements require careful negotiation to ensure that CDMOs bear appropriate financial responsibility for quality failures and regulatory non-compliance. Blanket liability caps and broad exclusions of consequential damages can create perverse incentives and leave Ceritas exposed to significant unrecovered losses in the event of a quality failure.

489	**[15.1 Mandatory Position --- Carve-Outs]{.underline}**
490	
491	No liability cap shall apply to claims arising from: (a) quality failures (including failures to comply with cGMP, product specifications, or the Quality Agreement), (b) regulatory non-compliance, (c) intellectual property infringement, or (d) breaches of confidentiality obligations.
492	
493	Blanket liability caps that apply to quality and regulatory obligations --- i.e., caps that do not exclude the categories listed above --- are unacceptable. If the CDMO proposes a general liability cap, that cap must contain express carve-outs for each of the categories listed in this Section 15.1.
494	
495	Any mutual exclusion of consequential damages must similarly carve out the following categories of damages, which shall remain recoverable notwithstanding any exclusion of consequential damages:
496	
497	> • Costs of product recalls and field alerts, including all direct and indirect costs described in Section 10.3
498	>
499	> • Regulatory fines, penalties, and assessments
500	>
501	> • Third-party product-liability claims and associated defense costs
502	>
503	> • Lost profits directly attributable to CDMO quality failures that result in product supply interruption
504	
505	**[15.2 Preferred Position --- Cap Threshold]{.underline}**
506	
507	To the extent that a general liability cap exists for non-carved-out matters (i.e., matters not falling within the categories identified in Section 15.1), the cap must be no less than **200% of annual fees** payable to the CDMO under the MSA. 511	At the Fallback Position, the general liability cap (for non-carved-out matters) may be reduced to no less than **150% of annual MSA fees** (currently \$12,600,000 based on Year 1 fees), with all carve-outs specified in Section 15.1 remaining **non-negotiable**. 515	The selection of governing law and dispute-resolution mechanisms for the Quality Agreement has practical implications for enforceability, predictability, and Ceritas\'s ability to protect its interests in the event of a dispute. 542

547	> • Batch-record maintenance and records-retention obligations (Section 12)
548	>
549	> • Regulatory inspection cooperation obligations (Section 9)
550	>
551	> • Product-safety notifications, including recall cooperation and field-alert reporting (Section 10)
552	>
553	> • Complaint-handling investigation obligations (Section 18)

555	> • Data-integrity program obligations (Section 12)

569	At the Fallback Position, the **carve-out of quality and regulatory obligations from force-majeure relief remains non-negotiable**, as does the requirement for a documented business-continuity plan and disaster-recovery plan. 583	> • Investigation timelines (as specified in Section 18.2)
584	>
585	> • Trending requirements, including the frequency and format of complaint-trend reports
586	>
587	> • Escalation procedures for complaints that may involve patient safety, regulatory reporting obligations, or potential recall triggers
588	>
589	> • Requirements for retention of complaint samples, investigation records, and supporting documentation
590	
591	The complaint-handling annex is one of the four required annexes specified in Section 3.3 of this Playbook. Its inclusion is non-negotiable.
592	
593	**[18.2 Mandatory Position --- Investigation Timelines]{.underline}**
594	
595	The CDMO must initiate an investigation of each product-quality complaint within **3 business days** of receipt of the complaint (if received directly by the CDMO from a market source) or within 3 business days of notification from Ceritas (if the complaint is forwarded by Ceritas). \"Initiate\" means that the CDMO has opened an investigation record, assigned an investigator, and commenced the collection of relevant data, batch records, and retained samples.
