597	The CDMO must provide **preliminary findings** to Ceritas within **10 business days** of initiation of the investigation. Preliminary findings must include: (a) a summary of the complaint, (b) a description of the investigation activities conducted to date, (c) any preliminary root-cause hypotheses, and (d) an assessment of whether the complaint may warrant a field alert, recall, or regulatory notification.
598	
599	The **final investigation report** is due within **30 business days** of initiation of the investigation, unless an extension is granted in writing by Ceritas QA. Extension requests must include a description of the reason for the delay, a summary of the investigation status, and a proposed revised completion date.
600	
601	**[18.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
602	
603	Under the Preferred Position, the CDMO must forward any product-quality complaint received directly from a market source (e.g., a customer, distributor, healthcare professional, or patient) to Ceritas within **24 hours** of receipt. This ensures that Ceritas has early visibility into all complaint activity and can assess the need for regulatory reporting, trend analysis, or escalation.
604	
605	In addition, Ceritas retains the authority to direct the **scope and depth** of the investigation. This includes the right to require additional testing, expanded batch reviews, extended investigations, or the engagement of external experts, as Ceritas deems necessary based on the nature and severity of the complaint.
606	
607	**[18.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
608	
609	At the Fallback Position, the investigation initiation timeline may be extended to **5 business days**, and the preliminary findings timeline may be extended to **15 business days**, in each case with documented justification in the negotiation file. The final investigation report deadline remains at 30 business days.
610	
611	The requirement for a complaint-handling annex remains **non-negotiable** at the Fallback Position. Any Quality Agreement that omits a complaint-handling annex falls below the Fallback Position and may not be executed.
612	
613	**[19. Term, Termination, and Survival]{.underline}**
614	
615	The term, termination, and survival provisions of the Quality Agreement must be carefully aligned with the MSA and must ensure that quality obligations remain enforceable for an extended period following the conclusion of the business relationship.
616	
617	**[19.1 Term --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
618	
619	The Quality Agreement must be **coterminous with the MSA** --- that is, the Quality Agreement commences on the effective date of the MSA (or the date of first commercial manufacture, if later) and remains in effect for so long as the MSA remains in effect, terminating automatically upon termination or expiration of the MSA (subject to survival provisions).
620	
621	Independent fixed terms (e.g., a 5-year term with automatic renewal) create a risk of misalignment between the Quality Agreement and the MSA. If the MSA terminates or expires while the Quality Agreement remains in effect, the parties may face conflicting obligations. Conversely, if the Quality Agreement expires before the MSA, there may be a gap during which manufacturing or testing activities are conducted without a governing quality agreement --- an unacceptable regulatory risk.
622	
623	Automatic renewal provisions, if included, must mirror the renewal terms of the MSA. Standalone auto-renewal clauses that operate independently of the MSA must be removed or modified to align with the MSA term.
624	
625	**[19.2 Survival --- Mandatory Position]{.underline}**
626	
627	Quality-related obligations must survive termination or expiration of the Quality Agreement for a period of **10 years**. The surviving obligations must include, at a minimum:
628	
629	> • Records retention obligations (Section 12.2)
630	>
631	> • Cooperation with recalls and field alerts (Section 10)
632	>
633	> • Regulatory inspection support and cooperation (Section 9)
634	>
635	> • Complaint-handling cooperation (Section 18)
636	>
637	> • Data-integrity program maintenance for retained records (Section 12.1)
638	
639	Survival provisions that limit surviving obligations to records retention only, or that impose survival periods shorter than 10 years, are unacceptable. The 10-year period reflects the extended lifecycle of pharmaceutical products, the potential for latent quality issues to surface years after manufacture, and the regulatory expectation that NDA holders and MAHs maintain access to quality records and CDMO cooperation for an extended period.
640	
641	**[19.3 Preferred Position]{.underline}**
642	
643	Under the Preferred Position, **confidentiality obligations** also survive for 10 years post-termination. This ensures that sensitive information exchanged during the course of the quality-agreement relationship --- including Ceritas proprietary manufacturing processes, specifications, analytical methods, and regulatory strategy --- remains protected for a period consistent with the survival of quality obligations.
644	
645	**[19.4 Fallback Position]{.underline}**
646	
647	The **10-year survival period** for quality obligations is non-negotiable and may not be reduced. The scope of surviving obligations described in Section 19.2 is also non-negotiable. There is no Fallback Position that permits a shorter survival period or a narrower scope of surviving obligations.
648	
649	**[20. Exception and Escalation Procedures]{.underline}**
650	
651	The exception and escalation procedures set forth in this Section ensure that deviations from the Playbook are properly authorized, documented, and tracked.
652	
653	**[20.1 Mandatory Position Exceptions]{.underline}**
654	
655	Any concession below a **Mandatory Position** requires a **joint written exception** signed by both of the following individuals:
656	
657	> • **Dr. Mariel Castaño-Webb**, Vice President, Quality Assurance
658	>
659	> • **Jonathan R. Hadley**, Associate General Counsel, Commercial Transactions
660	
661	The joint written exception must include: (a) identification of the specific Playbook provision at issue, (b) a description of the proposed concession and the counterparty\'s rationale, (c) a risk assessment evaluating the impact of the concession on product quality, regulatory compliance, and patient safety, (d) identification of any compensating controls that will be implemented to mitigate the risk associated with the concession, and (e) the signatures of both approvers. The signed exception must be retained in the negotiation file.
662	
663	**[20.2 Fallback Position Exceptions]{.underline}**
664	
665	Any concession below a **Fallback Position** requires **written approval** from a **Senior Vice President or above**. The approval must be supported by a documented risk assessment prepared jointly by Quality Assurance and Legal. The risk assessment must address the same elements identified in Section 20.1 and must also include a recommendation from the Playbook Owner as to whether the concession should be approved or denied. The signed approval and supporting risk assessment must be retained in the negotiation file.
666	
667	**[20.3 Tracking]{.underline}**
668	
669	All exceptions and escalations --- regardless of the tier at which they arise --- are tracked in the **Quality Agreement Negotiation Log** maintained by the Playbook Owner. The Negotiation Log serves as a centralized record of all negotiation decisions that deviate from the Playbook, facilitating trend analysis, post-negotiation review, and audit readiness. The Playbook Owner reviews the Negotiation Log on a quarterly basis and reports the status of open and resolved exceptions to the Senior Vice President, Quality & Regulatory.

64	
65	**[Section 1 --- Purpose]{.underline}**
66	
67	**1.1** This Contract Deviation Risk Rating Rubric (the \"Rubric\") establishes the standardized methodology by which Ceritas Therapeutics, Inc. (\"Ceritas\") quality and legal reviewers assess, score, and label deviations identified when reviewing counterparty-drafted quality agreements against the Ceritas Quality Agreement Playbook (Document QA-PB-2024-003, as revised from time to time) (the \"Playbook\"). The Rubric provides a repeatable, objective framework so that every deviation receives consistent risk characterization regardless of which reviewer conducts the analysis or which counterparty presented the draft.
68	
69	**1.2** The Rubric is intended to ensure uniform, reproducible risk characterization across all contract development and manufacturing organization (\"CDMO\") and contract-laboratory quality agreement reviews conducted by or on behalf of Ceritas. By assigning each deviation a quantitative Composite Risk Score and a corresponding qualitative Risk Rating, the Rubric enables Ceritas negotiators to prioritize issues, allocate negotiation capital efficiently, and communicate risk posture to senior leadership in a consistent format.
70	
71	**1.3** The Rubric applies to all quality agreements required under commercial manufacturing, packaging, testing, and storage master service agreements (\"MSAs\") to which Ceritas is or will become a party. This includes quality agreements entered into with primary CDMOs, secondary CDMOs, contract packaging sites, contract analytical testing laboratories, stability-testing facilities, and third-party warehousing and distribution sites where such facilities perform quality-impacting activities on behalf of Ceritas.
72	
73	**1.4** This document contains methodology and definitions only. Provision-specific analyses---including individual deviation assessments, recommended redline positions, negotiation strategy recommendations, and business-justification memoranda---are documented separately in the Issues List and Risk Memorandum prepared for each quality agreement engagement. The Rubric does not prescribe specific substantive positions on any quality agreement provision; those positions are set forth exclusively in the Playbook.
74	
75	**1.5** All Ceritas personnel involved in quality agreement review, negotiation, or approval are expected to be trained on this Rubric prior to performing deviation assessments. Training records shall be maintained in the Ceritas Learning Management System in accordance with the Quality Systems training SOP (QA-SOP-2023-015).
76	
77	**[Section 2 --- Scope of Application]{.underline}**
78	
79	**2.1** This Rubric covers every identified deviation arising from the comparison of a counterparty-drafted quality agreement against the applicable Playbook positions. For purposes of this Rubric, the term \"deviation\" encompasses each of the following categories:
80	
81	> **(a)** Provisions in the counterparty draft that contradict a Playbook mandatory position---that is, provisions whose substance is directly contrary to, or materially inconsistent with, a position designated as mandatory in the Playbook;
82	>
83	> **(b)** Provisions in the counterparty draft that fall below a Playbook preferred position---that is, provisions that, while not necessarily contradicting a mandatory requirement, do not meet the standard that Ceritas considers its desired commercial and quality benchmark;
84	>
85	> **(c)** Provisions that are missing from the counterparty draft but that the Playbook requires to be present in the quality agreement (referred to herein as \"Missing Protections\")---including, without limitation, provisions addressing batch disposition authority, deviation and out-of-specification notification obligations, annual product quality review responsibilities, regulatory inspection cooperation, and recall decision-making authority; and
86	>
87	> **(d)** Terms that are non-market or commercially unusual for pharmaceutical quality agreements (referred to herein as \"Off-Market Terms\"), regardless of whether the Playbook expressly addresses the specific provision, including terms whose substance materially departs from customary pharmaceutical-industry quality agreement practice as understood by Ceritas\'s quality and legal professionals based on their collective experience and available industry benchmarks.
88	
89	**2.2** For the avoidance of doubt, the Rubric applies to deviations identified in quality agreements associated with both domestic (United States) and international manufacturing, packaging, testing, and storage operations. Where a quality agreement is governed by or must satisfy European Union GMP requirements, references in the Rubric to United States regulatory standards (e.g., 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211) shall be read to include the analogous EU requirements (e.g., EU GMP Annex 16, EudraLex Volume 4) as applicable.
90	
91	**2.3** The following agreement types are expressly excluded from the scope of this Rubric and are governed by separate, purpose-specific risk rating rubrics maintained by the responsible functional areas:
92	
93	> **(a)** Supply agreements and commercial supply terms embedded within MSAs (governed by Commercial Legal\'s Supply Agreement Deviation Rubric, Document CL-RB-2024-002);
94	>
95	> **(b)** Pharmacovigilance agreements and safety data exchange agreements (governed by Drug Safety\'s Pharmacovigilance Agreement Rubric, Document DS-RB-2024-001); and
96	>
97	> **(c)** Clinical-trial quality agreements associated with investigational product manufacturing (governed by Clinical Quality\'s Clinical QA Deviation Rubric, Document CQ-RB-2024-001).
98	
99	**2.4** Where a single counterparty agreement combines quality agreement provisions with supply terms or other out-of-scope provisions, this Rubric applies only to those sections of the agreement that address quality-related responsibilities, authorities, and obligations. Out-of-scope provisions within such combined agreements should be assessed under the applicable separate rubric, and the results of both assessments should be consolidated in the engagement\'s Risk Memorandum to provide a complete risk profile to decision-makers.
100	
101	**[Section 3 --- Definitions]{.underline}**
102	
103	The following terms, when used in this Rubric, have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Section have the meanings assigned to them elsewhere in this document or, if not defined herein, in the Playbook.
104	
105	**3.1 \"Deviation\"** means any difference between a counterparty\'s draft quality agreement provision and the corresponding Ceritas Playbook position, whether such position is designated as mandatory, preferred, or fallback. A Deviation includes, without limitation, a substantive contradiction, a weakened standard, a narrowed scope, an extended timeline, a shifted responsibility, or any other material departure from the Playbook\'s articulated position on a given topic. A single provision in the counterparty draft may give rise to more than one Deviation if it departs from the Playbook in multiple independent respects.
106	
107	**3.2 \"Mandatory Position\"** means a Playbook requirement from which no departure is permitted without the prior written exception of the VP, Quality Assurance and the concurrence of the General Counsel (or their respective designees). Mandatory Positions are identified in the Playbook by a red-flag designation and represent non-negotiable quality and regulatory requirements. Mandatory Positions typically address matters directly affecting patient safety, product quality attributes, regulatory compliance, and Ceritas\'s ability to fulfill its obligations as the NDA holder or EU Marketing Authorization Holder.
108	
109	**3.3 \"Preferred Position\"** means a Playbook requirement representing Ceritas\'s desired commercial and quality standard for a given quality agreement provision. Departure from a Preferred Position requires documented business justification approved by the reviewer\'s functional manager. Preferred Positions are identified in the Playbook by a yellow-flag designation. Acceptance of a position below the Preferred Position but at or above the Fallback Position does not require VP-level or General Counsel approval, provided the business justification is documented in the Issues List.
110	
111	**3.4 \"Fallback Position\"** means the minimum acceptable alternative to a Mandatory Position or Preferred Position, as pre-approved in the Playbook. Fallback Positions represent the floor below which Ceritas will not accept a given provision without escalation to senior leadership. Not every Playbook provision has an associated Fallback Position; where no Fallback Position is specified, the Mandatory Position or Preferred Position, as applicable, serves as the minimum acceptable standard.
112	
113	**3.5 \"Missing Protection\"** means a provision required by the Playbook to appear in the quality agreement that is entirely absent from the counterparty draft. A Missing Protection is treated as a Deviation for purposes of this Rubric. The absence of a provision addressing a Playbook mandatory topic is presumptively scored at Severity Value 4 (Critical) under Section 4, subject to the reviewer\'s assessment of the specific facts and circumstances.
114	
115	**3.6 \"Off-Market Term\"** means a provision in the counterparty draft whose substance materially departs from customary pharmaceutical-industry quality agreement practice, regardless of whether the Playbook expressly addresses the specific provision. Determination of whether a term is Off-Market is made by the reviewer in the exercise of professional judgment, informed by the reviewer\'s experience, available industry surveys and benchmarks, and consultation with colleagues as appropriate. Off-Market Terms are subject to automatic escalation under Section 9.2.
116	
117	**3.7 \"Product Tier\"** means the internal Ceritas classification of a drug product\'s commercial and patient-safety criticality, designated as Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3. Product Tier assignments are made jointly by Commercial Operations and Quality Assurance in accordance with the criteria set forth in Section 7 of this Rubric and are recorded in the Ceritas Product Tier Register (Document QA-REG-2025-001).
118	
119	**3.8 \"Composite Risk Score\" or \"CRS\"** means the numerical value produced by the scoring methodology described in Section 8 of this Rubric for a given Deviation. The CRS is a quantitative indicator of relative risk and is used to assign the Deviation to one of the four Risk Rating bands defined in Section 8.3.
120	
121	**3.9 \"Reviewer\"** means the Ceritas quality professional or legal professional who is applying this Rubric to assess and score a Deviation. More than one Reviewer may assess the same Deviation; where Reviewers\' scores differ, the higher score governs unless the Reviewers agree on a reconciled score and document their rationale.
122	
123	**[Section 4 --- Severity Tier Definitions]{.underline}**
124	
125	**4.1 General.** Each Deviation identified during the quality agreement review process is assigned to one of four severity tiers. The severity tier reflects the inherent seriousness of the Deviation---that is, the nature and magnitude of the risk that the Deviation introduces or fails to mitigate---without regard to the probability that the risk will materialize. Probability is addressed separately through the Likelihood Assessment in Section 6. Each severity tier carries a Severity Value that is used as a factor in the quantitative Composite Risk Score calculation described in Section 8.
126	
127	**4.2 Severity Tier Descriptions.** The four severity tiers, together with their assigned Severity Values and illustrative examples, are set forth below.
128	
129	**4.2.1 Severity Value 4 --- Critical**
130	
131	A Deviation is classified as Critical when it directly implicates patient safety, product quality (including the identity, strength, purity, or potency of the drug product), or creates material exposure to regulatory enforcement action, including but not limited to the issuance of a warning letter, entry of a consent decree, or the triggering of recall liability. A Deviation is also classified as Critical when the counterparty draft entirely omits a Playbook mandatory provision (i.e., a Missing Protection involving a mandatory topic), because the absence of such a provision leaves Ceritas without a contractually enforceable right or obligation that Ceritas considers essential to its quality system.
132	
133	Illustrative examples of Critical Deviations include, but are not limited to:
134	
135	> • Absence of Ceritas final batch disposition authority, or language that grants final disposition authority to the CDMO without Ceritas approval or concurrent release;
136	>
137	> • Removal or material limitation of Ceritas\'s sole recall decision-making authority, including provisions that grant the CDMO the right to initiate or veto a recall without Ceritas concurrence;
138	>
139	> • Absence of deviation-notification obligations, or notification timelines that are so extended as to effectively eliminate Ceritas\'s ability to assess product impact in a timely manner;
140	>
141	> • Liability caps that extinguish meaningful recourse for quality failures, including caps set at levels that would not cover the cost of a single product recall or regulatory remediation effort;
142	>
143	> • Absence of provisions requiring the CDMO to notify Ceritas of regulatory inspections or to permit Ceritas participation in inspection-related activities;
144	>
145	> • Elimination or material restriction of Ceritas\'s right to audit the CDMO\'s manufacturing facility, quality systems, or records; and
146	>
147	> • Provisions purporting to disclaim the CDMO\'s responsibility for compliance with applicable current Good Manufacturing Practice (\"cGMP\") requirements.
148	
149	**4.2.2 Severity Value 3 --- Major**
150	
151	A Deviation is classified as Major when it materially weakens Ceritas\'s oversight of the counterparty\'s quality-impacting activities, extends timelines for quality-critical notifications or actions beyond the Playbook fallback positions, or shifts decision-making authority to the counterparty for quality-impacting activities without adequate safeguards to protect Ceritas\'s interests as the product owner and regulatory filing holder. Major Deviations do not directly eliminate Ceritas\'s rights or protections but substantially degrade them.
152	
153	Illustrative examples of Major Deviations include, but are not limited to:
154	
155	> • Change-control notice periods that are shorter than the Playbook fallback position (e.g., the counterparty draft provides 15 calendar days\' prior notice of a planned change where the Playbook fallback requires 30 calendar days);
156	>
157	> • CAPA approval authority retained entirely by the counterparty, with Ceritas afforded input or consultation rights only rather than approval or concurrence rights;
158	>
159	> • Regulatory inspection notification delayed well beyond 24 hours (e.g., the counterparty draft requires notification within 5 business days rather than within 24 hours of the CDMO\'s receipt of notice of the inspection);
160	>
161	> • Annual product quality review (\"APQR\") preparation responsibilities assigned solely to the CDMO without a requirement for Ceritas review and approval prior to finalization;
162	>
163	> • Provisions that permit the CDMO to use subcontractors for quality-impacting activities without Ceritas\'s prior written consent; and
164	>
165	> • Qualification and validation responsibilities allocated without clear delineation, creating ambiguity regarding which party is responsible for critical process validation activities.
166	
167	**4.2.3 Severity Value 2 --- Moderate**
168	
169	A Deviation is classified as Moderate when it departs from a Playbook preferred position (but not a mandatory position), or when it meets the Playbook fallback position but introduces operational inconvenience, information-access delays, or other friction that, while manageable, is not aligned with Ceritas\'s preferred operating model. A Moderate classification is also assigned to Missing Protections involving annexes or exhibits whose absence does not independently create a compliance gap but reduces clarity, completeness, or enforceability of the quality agreement.
170	
171	Illustrative examples of Moderate Deviations include, but are not limited to:
172	
173	> • Raw data turnaround timelines that are longer than the Playbook preferred position but remain within a range that Ceritas quality operations can accommodate without jeopardizing regulatory submission timelines (e.g., 20 business days where the Playbook prefers 10 business days but the fallback permits up to 25 business days);
174	>
175	> • APQR submission deadlines that extend beyond the Playbook preferred timeline but remain within one additional calendar month;
176	>
177	> • Absence of a dedicated contact-list annex where the body of the agreement nonetheless contains general contact obligations;
178	>
179	> • Provisions that require Ceritas to provide written notice of audit requests further in advance than the Playbook prefers but within a timeframe that does not materially impair Ceritas\'s ability to conduct timely audits; and
180	>
181	> • Definition of \"confidential information\" that is narrower than Ceritas\'s preferred scope but still covers quality-related data and regulatory submissions.
182	
183	**4.2.4 Severity Value 1 --- Minor**
184	
185	A Deviation is classified as Minor when it is largely administrative, presentational, or terminological in nature and does not materially affect Ceritas\'s quality oversight, regulatory posture, or commercial protection. Minor Deviations may be noted in the Issues List for completeness but typically do not warrant negotiation capital.
186	
187	Illustrative examples of Minor Deviations include, but are not limited to:
188	
189	> • Formatting differences in contact lists (e.g., the counterparty draft presents contacts in a different table format than the Playbook template);
190	>
191	> • Minor differences in defined-term usage that do not change the substantive meaning of the provision (e.g., the counterparty draft uses \"Manufacturing Site\" where the Playbook uses \"Facility,\" but the defined scope is identical);
192	>
193	> • Numbering or cross-referencing conventions that differ from Ceritas\'s preferred format;
194	>
195	> • Non-substantive variations in the ordering of provisions within the agreement; and
196	>
197	> • Differences in the title or heading of the agreement itself (e.g., \"Quality Technical Agreement\" rather than \"Quality Agreement\").
198	
199	**4.3 Severity Classification Guidance.** Where a Deviation does not clearly fall within a single severity tier, the Reviewer should assign the higher of the two tiers under consideration and document the rationale for the classification in the Issues List. This approach reflects the Rubric\'s conservative design philosophy: in cases of ambiguity, Ceritas\'s risk framework favors the more protective classification.
200	
201	**[Section 5 --- Impact Assessment Criteria]{.underline}**
202	
203	**5.1 General.** In addition to the Severity Value assigned under Section 4, each Deviation is assessed against four discrete impact domains. The impact assessment evaluates the consequences that would follow if the Deviation were accepted in the executed quality agreement and the risk it introduces were to materialize. Each impact domain is scored on a four-point scale (1 through 4), with 4 representing the most severe impact and 1 representing the least severe impact. The scoring descriptors for each domain are set forth below.
204	
205	The Reviewer must assess and score each of the four impact domains independently. The purpose of the multi-domain assessment is to capture the full spectrum of consequences associated with a given Deviation, recognizing that a single Deviation may have different levels of impact across patient safety, regulatory compliance, commercial exposure, and operational oversight.
206	
207	After scoring all four domains, the Reviewer identifies the **Highest Domain Score** across Patient Safety and Product Quality Impact (PS), Regulatory Compliance Impact (RC), Commercial and Financial Impact (CF), and Operational Oversight Impact (OO). This highest score is designated the **Impact Value (IV)** for that Deviation and is used in the Composite Risk Score calculation described in Section 8.
208	
209	**5.2 Patient Safety and Product Quality Impact (PS)**
210	
211	This domain evaluates whether the Deviation, if the associated risk materializes, could affect the safety of patients receiving Ceritas drug products or the quality attributes (identity, strength, purity, potency, and stability) of those products.

216	  **4**                   Direct risk to patient safety or product quality attributes                               The Deviation, if accepted and the risk materializes, would create a direct and proximate risk that a drug product reaching patients could be adulterated, misbranded, sub-potent, contaminated, or otherwise not conforming to its approved specifications. This score is also appropriate where the Deviation would impair Ceritas\'s ability to detect or respond to a quality event that poses patient risk.

218	  **3**                   Indirect risk through weakened quality controls                                           The Deviation would not directly cause a product quality failure but would weaken one or more quality controls (e.g., CAPA effectiveness verification, environmental monitoring review, deviation trending) such that a quality failure could develop or persist undetected for longer than it would under the Playbook standard.

273	**5.6 Impact Value Determination.** As noted above, the Impact Value (IV) for a given Deviation is the highest score recorded across the four impact domains (PS, RC, CF, and OO). This approach ensures that a Deviation is characterized by its most consequential impact dimension. For example, a Deviation that scores PS = 2, RC = 4, CF = 2, and OO = 3 would receive an Impact Value of 4, reflecting the critical regulatory compliance concern even though the patient safety and commercial impacts are lower.
274	
275	**[Section 6 --- Likelihood Assessment Criteria]{.underline}**
276	
277	**6.1 General.** The Likelihood Assessment evaluates the probability that a given Deviation, if accepted in the executed quality agreement, would result in the harm identified in the Impact Assessment during the term of the agreement (including any renewal or extension periods, as applicable). Likelihood is scored on a four-point scale. The Reviewer should consider the specific operational context of the quality agreement, the historical performance profile of the counterparty (if known), the nature of the manufacturing or testing activities covered by the agreement, and general industry experience when assigning the Likelihood Score.
278	
279	**6.2 Likelihood Scale.** The four-point Likelihood Scale is defined as follows:
280	
281	**6.2.1 Likelihood Score 4 --- Almost Certain**
282	
283	The scenario giving rise to harm has occurred in prior Ceritas CDMO relationships or is an inherent feature of ongoing manufacturing, packaging, testing, or storage operations. A score of 4 is appropriate when the triggering event is essentially inevitable during the agreement term. For example, manufacturing deviations will occur at any operating facility; regulatory inspections of active pharmaceutical manufacturing sites will occur; the CDMO will initiate change controls during the term of a multi-year agreement. Where the Deviation relates to Ceritas\'s rights or protections in connection with events that are certain or near-certain to occur, the Likelihood Score should be 4.
284	
285	**6.2.2 Likelihood Score 3 --- Likely**
286	
287	The scenario giving rise to harm is expected to arise based on industry experience or the specific CDMO\'s operational profile, even though it is not a certainty. A score of 3 is appropriate when, for example, the CDMO has a history of quality observations or regulatory findings, or when the manufacturing process involves known areas of complexity or variability that make quality events probable. Events such as out-of-specification results during routine testing, or the need to conduct a field alert or market action, would generally be scored as Likely for CDMOs operating at commercial scale.
288	
289	**6.2.3 Likelihood Score 2 --- Possible**
290	
291	The scenario giving rise to harm could arise but is not routine and is dependent on contingent events that may or may not occur during the agreement term. A score of 2 is appropriate for events such as a significant product recall, a consent decree, or a major facility shutdown---events that are within the realm of possibility but that do not occur with regularity in the CDMO\'s operational history or in the industry generally for the type of manufacturing at issue.
292	
293	**6.2.4 Likelihood Score 1 --- Remote**
294	
295	The scenario giving rise to harm is theoretically possible but unlikely during the agreement term under foreseeable circumstances. A score of 1 is reserved for low-probability, high-impact events such as a complete facility destruction, a counterparty insolvency accompanied by immediate cessation of operations, or an unprecedented regulatory action without prior warning. The Reviewer should exercise caution in assigning a Likelihood Score of 1 and should document the basis for concluding that the triggering scenario is truly remote.
296	
297	**6.3 Interaction with Impact Assessment.** The Likelihood Score is independent of the Impact Value. A Deviation may have a very high Impact Value (e.g., 4) but a low Likelihood Score (e.g., 1) if the triggering scenario is remote. Conversely, a Deviation with a moderate Impact Value (e.g., 2) may have a high Likelihood Score (e.g., 4) if the triggering event is virtually certain. The Composite Risk Score formula in Section 8 integrates both dimensions to produce a balanced risk characterization.
298	
299	**[Section 7 --- Product-Tier Weighting]{.underline}**
300	
301	**7.1 General.** The scoring methodology applies a Product-Tier Multiplier (\"PTM\") that adjusts the Composite Risk Score to reflect the commercial and patient-safety criticality of the drug product covered by the quality agreement under review. The rationale for product-tier weighting is straightforward: a Deviation in a quality agreement governing the manufacture of Ceritas\'s most commercially important and patient-critical product warrants greater risk sensitivity than the identical Deviation in a quality agreement governing a mature product with ample therapeutic alternatives and modest revenue contribution.
302	
303	**7.2 Product-Tier Definitions and Multipliers.** The three product tiers and their corresponding PTMs are set forth below:
304	
305	**7.2.1 Tier 1 --- Critical Revenue Product (PTM = 1.5)**
306	
307	Tier 1 is assigned to drug products representing a significant revenue contribution to Ceritas or serving patient populations with limited therapeutic alternatives. Tier 1 products are those for which a supply disruption, quality failure, or regulatory action would have a disproportionate impact on Ceritas\'s commercial performance, patient access, or corporate reputation. As of the effective date of this Rubric, Velorantib Tablets (25 mg and 100 mg) carry a Tier 1 classification, reflecting their status as Ceritas\'s primary commercial product and the limited availability of therapeutic alternatives for the indicated patient population.
308	
309	The PTM of 1.5 amplifies the Composite Risk Score for any Deviation in a quality agreement covering a Tier 1 product by 50%, reflecting the elevated consequences of risk materialization.
310	
311	**7.2.2 Tier 2 --- Significant Product (PTM = 1.25)**
312	
313	Tier 2 is assigned to marketed drug products with moderate revenue contribution and for which therapeutic alternatives are available to patients. Tier 2 products are commercially important to Ceritas but do not carry the heightened patient-access or revenue-criticality profile of Tier 1 products. A supply disruption or quality failure involving a Tier 2 product, while serious, would not have the same magnitude of impact as a comparable event involving a Tier 1 product.
314	
315	The PTM of 1.25 amplifies the Composite Risk Score for any Deviation in a quality agreement covering a Tier 2 product by 25%.
316	
317	**7.2.3 Tier 3 --- Standard Product (PTM = 1.0)**
318	
319	Tier 3 is assigned to mature or non-critical marketed drug products. Tier 3 products typically have established supply chains, multiple available therapeutic alternatives, and a revenue contribution that, while positive, does not drive Ceritas\'s financial performance. The risk profile associated with Deviations in Tier 3 quality agreements is evaluated without amplification.
320	
321	The PTM of 1.0 applies the Composite Risk Score without adjustment.
322	
323	**7.3 Product-Tier Assignment and Maintenance.** Product-tier assignments are made and maintained by Commercial Operations in coordination with Quality Assurance. The assignments are reviewed at least annually, or more frequently if warranted by a material change in a product\'s commercial profile (e.g., launch of a competitive product, significant change in revenue trajectory, or receipt of a new indication). Current product-tier assignments are recorded in the Ceritas Product Tier Register (Document QA-REG-2025-001), which is maintained by Commercial Operations and made available to all quality and legal reviewers who perform quality agreement deviation assessments.
324	
325	**7.4 Quality Agreements Covering Multiple Products.** Where a single quality agreement covers the manufacture, testing, or storage of products assigned to different product tiers, the PTM applied to a given Deviation is the PTM associated with the highest-tier product covered by the agreement, unless the Deviation is demonstrably limited in its application to a lower-tier product. In the latter case, the Reviewer may apply the product-specific PTM and must document the basis for doing so in the Issues List.
326	
327	**[Section 8 --- Composite Risk Score Calculation and Rating Assignment]{.underline}**
328	
329	**8.1 Calculation Formula**
330	
331	The Composite Risk Score (\"CRS\") for each Deviation is calculated using the following formula:
332	
333	**CRS = Severity Value (SV) × Impact Value (IV) × Likelihood Score (LS) × Product-Tier Multiplier (PTM)**
334	
335	Where:
336	
337	> • **Severity Value (SV)** is the numerical value (1, 2, 3, or 4) assigned under Section 4 based on the severity tier classification of the Deviation;
338	>
339	> • **Impact Value (IV)** is the highest domain score (1, 2, 3, or 4) across the four impact domains assessed under Section 5;
340	>
341	> • **Likelihood Score (LS)** is the numerical value (1, 2, 3, or 4) assigned under Section 6 based on the probability assessment; and
342	>
343	> • **Product-Tier Multiplier (PTM)** is the multiplier (1.0, 1.25, or 1.5) corresponding to the product tier assigned under Section 7.
344	
345	**8.2 Score Range**
346	
347	The CRS ranges from a theoretical minimum of **1.0** (calculated as 1 × 1 × 1 × 1.0, representing a Minor Deviation with the lowest impact, the most remote likelihood, and a Tier 3 product) to a theoretical maximum of **96.0** (calculated as 4 × 4 × 4 × 1.5, representing a Critical Deviation with the highest impact, an almost-certain likelihood, and a Tier 1 product).
348	
349	The following table illustrates selected CRS values across the scoring continuum:
350	
351	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
352	  **SV**      **IV**      **LS**      **PTM**     **CRS**     **Interpretation**
353	  ----------- ----------- ----------- ----------- ----------- ----------------------------------
354	  1           1           1           1.0         1.0         Minimal risk
355	
356	  2           2           2           1.0         8.0         Low risk
357	
358	  3           3           3           1.0         27.0        High risk
359	
360	  3           3           3           1.25        33.75       High risk (Tier 2 amplification)
361	
362	  4           4           3           1.5         72.0        Critical risk
363	
364	  4           4           4           1.5         96.0        Maximum critical risk
365	  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

367	**8.3 Risk Rating Bands**
368	
369	Based on its calculated CRS, each Deviation is assigned one of four Risk Ratings. The Risk Rating determines the negotiation posture, escalation requirements, and documentation obligations applicable to the Deviation. The four Risk Rating bands are as follows:
370	
371	**8.3.1 Critical Risk (Red) --- CRS ≥ 48.0.** A Deviation rated Critical Risk is unacceptable to Ceritas in its current form. The Deviation must be redlined to the Ceritas mandatory position as specified in the Playbook. Under no circumstances may the quality agreement be executed while a Critical Risk Deviation remains unresolved. Resolution requires either (a) the counterparty\'s acceptance of the Ceritas mandatory position or (b) a negotiated alternative that the VP, Quality Assurance and the Associate General Counsel jointly determine provides equivalent protection.
372	
373	A Critical Risk rating requires the direct engagement of the VP, Quality Assurance (Dr. Mariel Castaño-Webb) and the Associate General Counsel, Commercial Transactions (Jonathan R. Hadley) in the negotiation of the Deviation. The Reviewer must immediately notify both individuals upon assignment of a Critical Risk rating and must not transmit a redline to the counterparty until the VP, Quality Assurance and Associate General Counsel have reviewed and approved the proposed redline position.
374	
375	**8.3.2 High Risk (Orange) --- CRS 24.0 -- 47.9.** A Deviation rated High Risk presents serious concern and must be redlined to at least the Ceritas fallback position as specified in the Playbook. Execution of the quality agreement may proceed with a High Risk Deviation accepted at the fallback position (or above) only if the VP, Quality Assurance provides a documented exception. The documented exception must identify the Deviation, state the business justification for accepting the fallback or alternative position, and confirm that the accepted position does not create an unacceptable patient-safety, regulatory-compliance, or commercial risk.
376	
377	The Reviewer should prioritize High Risk Deviations in negotiation discussions and should clearly communicate to the counterparty that acceptance of the counterparty\'s position is not possible without senior-level approval.
378	
379	**8.3.3 Medium Risk (Yellow) --- CRS 10.0 -- 23.9.** A Deviation rated Medium Risk should be redlined to the Ceritas preferred position as specified in the Playbook. However, the Deviation may be accepted at the Reviewer\'s discretion---with documented rationale---if the counterparty resists the preferred position and a legitimate business justification supports acceptance. The documented rationale must be recorded in the Issues List and must address why the accepted position is operationally and commercially adequate notwithstanding the departure from the preferred standard.
380	
381	Medium Risk Deviations do not require VP-level or General Counsel escalation unless they also trigger one of the automatic escalation criteria set forth in Section 9.
382	
383	**8.3.4 Low Risk (Green) --- CRS \< 10.0.** A Deviation rated Low Risk is acceptable to Ceritas or may be raised as a commercial-improvement request at the Reviewer\'s discretion. No escalation is required. The Deviation should be recorded in the Issues List for traceability purposes but does not require negotiation capital to be expended unless the Reviewer determines that the improvement can be obtained without material concession.

473	**10.3 Retention.** All scoring records---including completed Issues Lists, Risk Memoranda, redline drafts, and supporting documentation (e.g., business justification memoranda, exception approvals)---must be retained for the longer of:

475	> **(a)** The term of the quality agreement to which they relate, plus the full duration of any post-termination survival period applicable to quality-related obligations under the governing MSA or the quality agreement itself; or
476	>
477	> **(b)** Ten (10) years from the date of the scoring assessment.
478	
479	Retention shall be consistent with the Ceritas Records Management Policy (Document ADM-POL-2023-008) and shall be effected through storage in the Ceritas Quality Management System document repository or such other repository as designated by the VP, Quality Assurance. Records must be retrievable upon request for purposes of regulatory inspection, internal audit, or management review.
480	
481	**[Section 11 --- Periodic Review of Rubric]{.underline}**
482	
483	**11.1 Review Frequency.** This Rubric is reviewed and, if necessary, revised at least annually by Quality Assurance in consultation with the Legal department. The annual review is intended to ensure that the Rubric remains current and effective in light of evolving regulatory requirements, industry practice, and Ceritas\'s accumulated experience in quality agreement negotiation and administration.
484	
485	**11.2 Review Considerations.** Each periodic review must account for, at a minimum, the following considerations:
486	
487	> **(a)** Changes in applicable regulatory guidance, including new or revised FDA guidance documents, EMA guidelines, and ICH guidelines that bear on quality agreement content or GMP expectations;
488	>
489	> **(b)** Trends observed in FDA and EMA inspections, including recurring observations or enforcement actions that suggest evolving regulatory expectations regarding quality agreement provisions;
490	>
491	> **(c)** Lessons learned from Ceritas\'s quality agreement negotiations conducted since the last Rubric revision, including recurring counterparty positions, negotiation outcomes, and any instances where the Rubric\'s scoring methodology produced results that did not accurately reflect the risk profile of a Deviation;
492	>
493	> **(d)** Changes to the Playbook, including the addition, modification, or removal of mandatory, preferred, or fallback positions;
494	>
495	> **(e)** Changes to Ceritas\'s product portfolio, including new product approvals, product discontinuations, and changes to product-tier assignments that may affect the Product-Tier Weighting methodology; and
496	>
497	> **(f)** Feedback from Reviewers, negotiation teams, and senior leadership regarding the Rubric\'s usability, clarity, and effectiveness.
498	
499	**11.3 Version Control.** This document is maintained under the Ceritas document control system. The current version is **Rev. 2**, effective **February 1, 2025**. The next scheduled review is **February 1, 2026**. All prior versions are archived and available for reference through the Ceritas Quality Management System document repository.
500	
501	**11.4 Interim Revisions.** Notwithstanding the annual review cycle, interim revisions to this Rubric may be issued at any time if warranted by a material change in regulatory requirements, a significant quality event, or other circumstances that render the current version inadequate. Interim revisions follow the same approval process as scheduled revisions and are reflected in the Revision History table on the cover page of this document.
502	
503	**--- END OF DOCUMENT ---**
504	
505	Document QA-RB-2024-010, Rev. 2 --- Effective February 1, 2025
506

This document is controlled when accessed electronically through the Ceritas Quality Management System. Printed copies are uncontrolled and may not reflect the current revision.

def _diff_words(a: str, b: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return word-level diff ops as (op, text) pairs. op ∈ {'eq', 'ins', 'del'}."""
    try:

                ops.append(("ins", " ".join(bw[j1:j2]) + " "))

83	Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with an updated list of designated Qualified Persons on an annual basis, and Annex A shall be updated accordingly. Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing of any proposed change to the designated QP or alternate QP at least thirty (30) calendar days before the effective date of the change. Such notice shall include the identity, qualifications, and relevant experience of the proposed replacement QP. Ceritas shall have the right to interview or otherwise assess the proposed replacement QP (in person, by videoconference, or by written questionnaire, at Ceritas\'s discretion) before the change takes effect, and to object in writing to the proposed change within such thirty (30)-day period. If Ceritas objects, Pinnacle shall not implement the change until the objection has been resolved to Ceritas\'s satisfaction. Where a QP change is required on an unplanned basis (for example, due to death, incapacity, or resignation with immediate effect), Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas within two (2) business days, the alternate QP shall act in the interim, and the permanent replacement shall be subject to Ceritas\'s rights under this Section 4.3. 90	
91	Changes to validated processes, equipment, facilities, materials, documentation, or any other element that could directly or indirectly affect the identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency of the Product shall be managed through Pinnacle\'s change-control system in compliance with cGMP requirements. Pinnacle shall maintain a documented change-control procedure that provides for the evaluation, classification, approval, implementation, and documentation of all proposed changes.
92	
93	Pinnacle\'s change-control system shall ensure that all proposed changes are assessed for their potential impact on the Product, including considerations related to product quality, process capability, validated state, regulatory compliance, and the need for regulatory submissions. Changes shall be classified and documented in accordance with Pinnacle\'s applicable SOPs.
94	
95	**5.2** **Prior** **Written Approval by Ceritas.**
96	
97	Pinnacle shall not implement any change to manufacturing process parameters, process steps, or in-process controls; equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packaging, or testing of the Product (including like-for-like equipment replacements); the Facility (including HVAC, water systems, clean-room classifications, and environmental monitoring programs); raw-material, excipient, or component suppliers (including any change in the grade, source, or synthesis route of any raw material or excipient); primary or secondary packaging components or suppliers; test methods, reference standards, or analytical instruments used for release or stability testing; or computerized systems used to control, monitor, or record GMP activities (including laboratory information management systems and manufacturing execution systems), in each case that could directly or indirectly affect the identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency of the Product or that may require a regulatory submission in any jurisdiction (each, a \"Significant Change\"), without the prior written approval of Ceritas.
98	
99	Pinnacle shall submit a complete change-notification package to Ceritas at least ninety (90) calendar days before the proposed implementation date of any Significant Change. The ninety (90)-day period shall commence upon Ceritas\'s receipt of a complete package, which shall include: (a) a description of the proposed change; (b) the rationale for the change; (c) a risk assessment evaluating the potential impact on Product quality and regulatory status (including the Marketing Authorisations); (d) proposed qualification and/or validation activities; and (e) a proposed implementation timeline. Ceritas shall provide its written approval, rejection, or request for additional information within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of a complete package, consistent with Section 3.5 of the MSA.
100	
101	No Significant Change shall be implemented without Ceritas\'s documented prior written approval. Ceritas\'s approval shall not relieve Pinnacle of its responsibility to implement the change in compliance with cGMP. Where a Significant Change requires a regulatory submission, Pinnacle shall not implement the change (or, as applicable, release Product manufactured, tested, or packaged using the change) until Ceritas has confirmed in writing that the applicable regulatory approval has been obtained or that the applicable regulatory notification or waiting period has elapsed.
102	
103	All proposed changes shall be classified as Critical, Major, or Minor in accordance with the Change Classification Matrix set forth in Annex F. Ceritas shall have sole authority to classify any change, and in the event of any disagreement regarding classification, Ceritas\'s classification shall prevail. Changes classified as Minor under Annex F that have no potential impact on the Product may be managed through Pinnacle\'s internal change-control system without prior Ceritas approval, provided that such changes are listed in the monthly quality summary report and the related change-control records are made available to Ceritas upon request and during audits. Like-for-like equipment replacements are not exempt from Ceritas approval unless expressly so classified in Annex F.
104	
105	**5.3 Ceritas-Initiated Changes.**
106	
107	Ceritas may request changes to the Specifications, test methods, packaging configurations, labeling, or other aspects of the Product or the manufacturing process by providing written notice to Pinnacle\'s quality contact. Such notice shall include a detailed description of the requested change, the rationale for the request, any supporting technical data or regulatory justification, and the desired timeline for implementation.
108	
109	Upon receipt of a Ceritas change request, Pinnacle shall evaluate the feasibility of the requested change, including an assessment of the potential impact on the manufacturing process, validated state, timeline, and cost. Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with a written assessment of the requested change within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request, which shall include Pinnacle\'s determination of feasibility, any technical concerns, an estimated timeline for implementation, and any cost implications (to the extent such cost matters are relevant under the MSA).
110	
111	Implementation of any Ceritas-initiated change shall be subject to mutual written agreement of the Parties and shall be carried out in accordance with Pinnacle\'s change-control procedures. Neither Party shall be obligated to agree to a requested change that it reasonably determines is not feasible, would have an adverse impact on product quality, or would otherwise be inconsistent with cGMP requirements; provided, however, that Pinnacle shall implement any change required by a Regulatory Authority, by the Marketing Authorisations, or by Applicable Law within the timeline so required (as notified by Ceritas), subject to the cost provisions of the MSA.
112	
113	**5.4 Regulatory Submissions.**
114	
115	Ceritas (or Ceritas Ireland, with respect to the EU Marketing Authorisation) shall be solely responsible for preparing, filing, and maintaining all regulatory submissions, supplements, variations, and annual reports arising from changes to the Product, the manufacturing process, the Specifications, or the Facility, including but not limited to Prior Approval Supplements, Changes Being Effected supplements, and Type IA/IB/II variations under EU procedures.
116	
117	Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with all supporting documentation, technical data, validation reports, and other information reasonably requested by Ceritas in connection with the preparation and filing of such regulatory submissions. Pinnacle shall provide such documentation within ten (10) business days following receipt of Ceritas\'s written request, or within such shorter period as is necessary to meet a deadline imposed by a Regulatory Authority, as notified by Ceritas.
118	
119	**5.5 Emergency Changes.**
120	
121	Where a change is necessary to address an immediate threat to patient safety, Product quality, or Facility safety that cannot reasonably wait for the prior-approval process set forth in Section 5.2, Pinnacle may implement the change with concurrent notice to Ceritas. Concurrent notice shall be provided by email to the designated Ceritas quality contact within four (4) hours of implementation, followed by a formal written change notification within twenty-four (24) hours. Pinnacle shall obtain Ceritas\'s formal written approval of the emergency change within five (5) business days of implementation. If Ceritas does not approve the emergency change, Pinnacle shall promptly reverse the change or implement an alternative approved by Ceritas, unless reversal would itself create a safety risk, in which case the Parties shall confer immediately to agree on a corrective course of action. No Batch affected by an emergency change shall be certified or released without Ceritas\'s prior written approval.
122	
123	**[SECTION 6 --- DEVIATIONS AND CORRECTIVE AND PREVENTIVE ACTIONS]{.underline}**
124	
125	**6.1 Deviation Reporting.**
126	
127	Pinnacle shall document, classify, and investigate all deviations from approved manufacturing procedures, Specifications, cGMP requirements, or other established quality standards that occur during the manufacture, testing, packaging, storage, or release of the Product. Deviations shall be classified in accordance with Pinnacle\'s deviation classification SOP as Critical Deviations, Major Deviations, or Minor Deviations, based on the assessed or potential impact on product quality, safety, and compliance and consistent with the definitions in Section 2. Ceritas may review and, by written notice, reclassify any deviation, and Ceritas\'s classification shall prevail. Where the classification of a deviation is uncertain, Pinnacle shall treat the deviation as being of the higher classification pending resolution.
128	
129	Pinnacle shall report deviations to Ceritas in accordance with the following notification timelines, in each case measured from Detection and irrespective of the date of classification:
130	
131	> \(a\) **Critical Deviations:** Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of Detection of a deviation that is, or may reasonably be, a Critical Deviation. Such notification shall include a preliminary description of the deviation, the Batch(es) affected, the preliminary impact assessment, and the immediate containment actions taken by Pinnacle. Pinnacle shall provide supplemental written updates to Ceritas as the investigation progresses, and in any event at least every five (5) business days until the investigation report is submitted under Section 6.2.
132	>
133	> \(b\) **Major Deviations:** Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within five (5) business days of Detection of a Major Deviation. Such notification shall include a description of the deviation, the Batch(es) affected, the preliminary impact assessment, and the containment actions taken. Major Deviations shall also be summarized in the monthly quality summary report, which shall supplement, and shall not replace, the event-driven notification required by this Section 6.1(b). The monthly quality summary shall include a description of each Major Deviation that occurred during the reporting period, the Batch(es) affected, the current status of the investigation, and any interim or final corrective actions.
134	>
135	> \(c\) **Minor Deviations:** **Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing of each Minor Deviation within five (5) business days of Detection, which notification may be given by means of a consolidated written deviation log transmitted to the Ceritas quality contact designated in Annex A.** Minor Deviations shall be documented by Pinnacle in accordance with its deviation management SOPs, and such documentation shall be available for review by Ceritas upon request and during audits conducted pursuant to Section 9 of this Quality Agreement.
136	
137	Initial notification of Critical Deviations and Major Deviations may be made by email to the designated Ceritas quality contact listed in Annex A, provided that a formal written deviation report follows within the timelines set forth in Section 6.2. Periodic summary reporting shall not be used as the sole or primary means of notification for any Critical Deviation or Major Deviation. No Batch affected by an open Critical Deviation or Major Deviation shall be certified, released, or shipped without Ceritas\'s prior written approval.
138	
139	**6.2 Deviation Investigation.**
140	
141	Pinnacle shall investigate all deviations in accordance with its internal standard operating procedures for deviation management and investigation. Each investigation shall be commensurate with the classification and potential impact of the deviation and shall include, as applicable, a root-cause analysis, an impact assessment (including an assessment of the impact on previously released Batches, if applicable), identification of corrective and preventive actions, and documentation of the investigation findings and conclusions.
142	
143	Pinnacle shall complete the root-cause analysis and investigation of, and submit a written investigation report to Ceritas for, (a) each Critical Deviation within fifteen (15) business days of Detection, and (b) each Major Deviation within thirty (30) business days of Detection. These timelines are maximum periods, and earlier submission is expected wherever feasible. Extensions may be granted only with the prior written approval of Ceritas QA. Any extension request shall be submitted before the applicable deadline and shall include (i) an explanation of the reason the timeline cannot be met, (ii) a summary of work completed to date, (iii) a proposed revised completion date, and (iv) any interim risk-mitigation measures implemented. Root-cause analyses shall be conducted using a structured methodology (e.g., Ishikawa diagram, 5 Whys, or fault-tree analysis) and shall be supported by objective data; conclusory statements of root cause without supporting evidence shall not be acceptable.
144	
145	**6.3 Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA).**
146	
147	Pinnacle shall develop, approve, and implement Corrective and Preventive Action plans for all deviations, as appropriate based on the classification and root-cause analysis findings. Pinnacle shall submit each proposed CAPA plan for a Critical Deviation or a Major Deviation to Ceritas for review and written approval before implementation. Ceritas\'s written approval shall be a condition precedent to the implementation of any CAPA plan for a Critical Deviation or a Major Deviation; provided that Pinnacle may implement immediate containment actions necessary to protect Product quality or patient safety pending such approval, with notice to Ceritas. Pinnacle may approve and implement CAPA plans for Minor Deviations, subject to Ceritas\'s review upon request, during audits, and in the APQR.
148	
149	Pinnacle shall perform CAPA effectiveness checks at the intervals and against the criteria specified in the approved CAPA plan and shall report the results of each effectiveness check for Critical Deviations and Major Deviations to Ceritas, with supporting data demonstrating the effectiveness (or lack thereof) of the implemented actions, within ten (10) business days of completion of each check. CAPA status shall also be summarized in the monthly quality summary report. Pinnacle shall maintain all CAPA records in accordance with cGMP requirements, and such records shall be available for review by Ceritas during audits conducted pursuant to Section 9.
150	
151	**6.4 Out-of-Specification and Out-of-Trend Results.**
152	
153	Pinnacle shall investigate all OOS Results and OOT Results obtained in the testing of the Product, API, Ceritas-Furnished Materials, and components in accordance with the FDA Guidance for Industry, Investigating Out-of-Specification (OOS) Test Results for Pharmaceutical Production, and Chapter 6 of the EU GMP Guidelines. Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation of any OOS Result or OOT Result (confirmation occurring upon completion of the initial laboratory assessment concluding that the result is not attributable to an assignable laboratory error), and within twenty-four (24) hours of Detection of any OOS Result or OOT Result relating to a Batch that has been released or distributed. OOS and OOT investigations shall be completed and reported to Ceritas within the timelines applicable to Critical Deviations under Section 6.2, unless Ceritas agrees in writing to apply the timelines applicable to Major Deviations. No Batch subject to an open OOS or OOT investigation shall be certified, released, or shipped.

156	
157	**7.1 Batch Disposition.**
158	
159	The Parties agree to the following framework for batch disposition and release of the Product:

164	>
165	> \(c\) **Certificate of Analysis:** Pinnacle shall prepare a Certificate of Analysis for each Batch and provide it to Ceritas with the batch release package and with each shipment of the Product. Each Certificate of Analysis shall contain all of the information required by Section 2.2, including the Product name and strength, Batch number, date of manufacture and expiry date, the results of all release tests listed in the Specifications, the specification limits for each test, a reference to the Approved Test Method used for each test, and a statement of Batch disposition. The Certificate of Analysis shall be signed and dated by an authorized representative of Pinnacle\'s quality assurance function and shall be provided in sufficient time to permit Ceritas\'s review prior to further distribution. Use of any test method other than an Approved Test Method, or any modification of an Approved Test Method, without Ceritas\'s prior written approval shall constitute a deviation reportable under Section 6.1.
166	>
167	> \(d\) **Raw Data:** Supporting raw data and analytical records underlying the Certificate of Analysis shall be made available by Pinnacle to Ceritas upon request. Pinnacle shall provide complete raw data packages (including chromatograms, spectra, raw instrument data and associated audit trails, and complete laboratory notebook entries) within two (2) business days of Pinnacle\'s receipt of Ceritas\'s written request. Raw data and analytical records may be provided in electronic format, subject to applicable data integrity and security requirements.
168	>
169	> \(e\) **Batch Release Package:** For each Batch, Pinnacle shall deliver to Ceritas a complete batch release package, including the Certificate of Analysis, the executed batch production and packaging records, a summary of all deviations, OOS Results, OOT Results, and change controls affecting the Batch, and, for EU-market Batches, the QP certificate, within ten (10) business days after completion of Pinnacle\'s quality assurance review of the Batch.
170	
171	**7.2 Rejected Batches.**
172	
173	In the event that a Batch of the Product fails to meet the Specifications or is otherwise determined by Pinnacle or Ceritas to be non-conforming, Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas of the failure within twenty-four (24) hours of Detection and shall initiate a deviation investigation in accordance with Section 6 of this Quality Agreement. Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with a written summary of the investigation findings, including the root cause (if determined), the impact assessment, and the proposed disposition of the rejected Batch.
174	
175	No rejected Batch shall be released for distribution without the written agreement of both Parties. Disposition of rejected Batches, including reprocessing, reworking, or destruction, shall be determined by Ceritas following consultation with Pinnacle, in accordance with cGMP requirements and the terms of the MSA. No rejected or non-conforming Batch shall be reprocessed or reworked except in accordance with a procedure approved in the applicable Marketing Authorisation (or a regulatory submission approved by the applicable Regulatory Authority) and with Ceritas\'s prior written approval.
176	
177	**[SECTION 8 --- ANNUAL PRODUCT QUALITY REVIEW]{.underline}**
178	
179	**8.1 APQR Preparation.**
180	
181	Pinnacle shall prepare a draft Annual Product Quality Review (\"APQR\") for the Product covering all Batches manufactured during the preceding calendar year. The draft APQR shall be submitted to Ceritas no later than forty-five (45) calendar days after the close of each calendar year (i.e., no later than February 14 of the following year for the immediately preceding calendar year).
182	
183	The APQR shall address, at a minimum, the following topics, consistent with 21 CFR 211.180(e), ICH Q10, and Chapter 1 of the EU GMP Guidelines:
184	
185	> \(a\) a summary of all Batches manufactured during the review period, including batch numbers, manufacturing dates, batch sizes, and disposition status, including any Batches that were rejected, reprocessed, or reworked;
186	>
187	> \(b\) an analysis of trends in critical quality attributes, critical in-process controls and process parameters, and finished-product release testing results;
188	>
189	> \(c\) a summary of all deviations (Critical, Major, and Minor) that occurred during the review period, all OOS Results and OOT Results and related investigations, including root-cause analysis findings and CAPA status and effectiveness;
190	>
191	> \(d\) a summary of all change controls implemented during the review period that relate to the Product, the manufacturing process, equipment, or the Facility;
192	>
193	> \(e\) a review of stability data obtained during the review period, including any out-of-trend or out-of-specification results;
194	>
195	> \(f\) a review of all Complaints related to the Product that were received and investigated during the review period;
196	>
197	> \(g\) a summary of the results of any regulatory inspections or Ceritas audits that occurred during the review period;
198	>
199	> \(h\) a review of qualification and validation activities (including process validation, cleaning validation, and equipment and computerized-system qualification) and of the status and adequacy of post-approval commitments and regulatory submissions relating to the Product;
200	>
201	> \(i\) an assessment of the overall quality performance of the Product and identification of any areas for continuous improvement; and
202	>
203	> \(j\) such other topics as may be required by applicable cGMP regulations or as mutually agreed by the Parties.
204	
205	**8.2 Review and Finalization.**
206	
207	Ceritas shall review the draft APQR provided by Pinnacle and shall provide written comments, questions, or requests for additional information within thirty (30) calendar days following receipt. Ceritas shall have the right to require revisions to the draft APQR before finalization. Pinnacle shall incorporate Ceritas\'s comments and submit a revised APQR within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of Ceritas\'s comments. The APQR shall not be final until approved in writing by Ceritas.
208	
209	The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to finalize the APQR in a timely manner and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. The final APQR shall be approved and signed by the designated quality representatives of both Parties. A copy of the finalized APQR shall be retained by each Party in accordance with the records retention obligations set forth in Section 12.3.
210	
211	**[SECTION 9 --- AUDITS AND REGULATORY INSPECTIONS]{.underline}**
212	
213	**9.1 Ceritas Audit Rights.**
214	
215	Ceritas shall have the right to conduct GMP audits of the Facility, without limitation as to frequency, upon ten (10) business days\' prior written notice to Pinnacle. Audits shall be conducted during the Facility\'s operating hours, including any shift during which Product-related operations are performed. The scope of any such audit shall include all areas of the Facility and all records, systems, and personnel involved in or relating to the manufacture, testing, packaging, labeling, storage, release, and shipment of the Product and to the performance of Pinnacle\'s obligations under this Quality Agreement. Pinnacle shall provide access to the Facility, qualified personnel, and all relevant GMP documentation during the audit, including batch records, deviation reports, CAPA files, training records, equipment qualification and process validation records, and data-integrity program documentation.
216	
217	In addition to the annual routine audit described above, Ceritas may conduct additional audits on a \"for cause\" basis in response to specific events, including but not limited to the occurrence of a Critical Deviation, a product recall, an adverse regulatory inspection finding or other significant regulatory action (such as the issuance of a Form FDA 483, Warning Letter, or Import Alert), a Complaint, an adverse trend in OOS Results, or other circumstances that, in Ceritas\'s reasonable judgment, warrant an audit of the Facility. Ceritas may conduct a \"for cause\" audit at any time upon not less than forty-eight (48) hours\' prior written notice to Pinnacle. A \"for cause\" audit shall not be subject to Pinnacle\'s agreement or confirmation of availability, and Pinnacle shall make the Facility, relevant personnel, and documentation available on the date and for the scope notified by Ceritas.
218	
219	Each audit shall be conducted by personnel designated by Ceritas who are qualified to conduct GMP audits. Ceritas\'s audit team may include Ceritas employees, consultants, or third-party auditors retained by Ceritas, provided that any such consultants or third-party auditors are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 8 of the MSA, executed before they are granted access to the Facility or to Pinnacle\'s Confidential Information.
220	
221	**9.2 Audit Reports.**
222	
223	Following the completion of any audit conducted pursuant to Section 9.1, Ceritas shall prepare a written audit report summarizing the findings, observations, and any recommendations arising from the audit. Ceritas shall provide the audit report to Pinnacle within thirty (30) business days of the completion of the audit.
224	
225	Pinnacle shall review the audit report and shall respond to any audit findings or observations within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of the audit report (or within ten (10) business days for any finding classified by Ceritas as critical). Pinnacle\'s response shall include, as applicable, an assessment of each finding, identification of the root cause (for significant findings), proposed corrective and preventive actions, and target completion dates for remediation. Pinnacle shall complete remediation by the target completion dates accepted by Ceritas and shall report progress in the monthly quality summary report until all findings are closed.
226

**9.3 Regulatory Inspections.**

Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of receiving notice of, or becoming aware of, any regulatory inspection (whether pre-announced or unannounced) by a Regulatory Authority of the Facility or of any Subcontractor performing activities for the Product, or that relates directly to the Product; in the case of an unannounced inspection, such notice shall be given within twenty-four (24) hours of the commencement of the inspection. Such notification shall include the identity of the inspecting Regulatory Authority, the scheduled dates of the inspection (if known), the announced or anticipated scope of the inspection, and any other relevant information available to Pinnacle.

Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with copies of all inspection observations issued by the Regulatory Authority (e.g., Form FDA 483 observations, EU GMP inspection reports or non-compliance statements, or equivalent documents) and all correspondence with the inspecting authority relating to the inspection within two (2) business days of issuance or receipt, and in any event within the twenty-four (24)-hour period required by Section 5.3 of the MSA for the matters described therein. Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with a draft of each proposed response to inspection observations that relate to or may affect the Product at least three (3) business days before the applicable submission deadline and shall not submit any such response without Ceritas\'s prior written approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas with a copy of each response as submitted.
