7	
8	Ceritas shall have the right to participate in and observe any regulatory inspection that relates to the Product or to the manufacturing line, testing laboratory, or area of the Facility used for the manufacture, testing, packaging, or storage of the Product, including the opening meeting, daily wrap-up meetings, and the closing meeting, and to provide back-room support, subject only to any restriction imposed by the inspecting Regulatory Authority. Pinnacle shall take all reasonable steps to facilitate Ceritas\'s participation, including requesting permission from the inspecting authority where required, and shall provide Ceritas with daily written updates during the inspection. Pinnacle shall host and manage inspections of the Facility in consultation with Ceritas, consistent with Section 5.4 of the MSA.
9	
10	**[SECTION 10 --- PRODUCT RECALL AND FIELD ALERTS]{.underline}**
11	
12	**10.1 Recall Decision-Making.**
13	
14	Ceritas shall have sole decision-making authority with respect to the initiation, scope, and conduct of any recall, market withdrawal, field correction, or field alert relating to the Product (including any Field Alert Report and any notification to EU competent authorities), acting on its own behalf and on behalf of Ceritas Ireland. Pinnacle shall not initiate any recall or other market action relating to the Product, or communicate with any Regulatory Authority regarding any such action, without Ceritas\'s prior written consent, except where such communication is required by Applicable Law, in which case Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas before making it (or, where prior notice is legally impossible, immediately thereafter). Pinnacle\'s obligation to cooperate with and implement any recall or market action directed by Ceritas or by a Regulatory Authority shall be immediate and unconditional, and shall not be subject to Pinnacle\'s agreement with Ceritas\'s decision or to the resolution of any dispute regarding cost allocation.
15	
16	Each Party shall notify the other Party within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any information or event that may give rise to the need for a product recall or field alert, including but not limited to the receipt of adverse event reports, product quality complaints, regulatory communications, or other information suggesting that the Product may not conform to its Specifications or may present a risk to patient safety.
17	
18	Without limiting the foregoing, Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas within twenty-four (24) hours of Detection of any information concerning any incident that causes the Product or its labeling to be mistaken for, or applied to, another article; any bacteriological contamination; any significant chemical, physical, or other change or deterioration in distributed Product; or any failure of one or more distributed Batches to meet the Specifications, together with all information reasonably necessary for Ceritas to submit any required Field Alert Report within three (3) working days as required by 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1) and to meet its EU reporting obligations.
19	
20	**10.2 Cost Allocation.**
21	
22	Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the costs and expenses associated with any product recall or field alert relating to the Product (including direct costs of notification, retrieval, destruction, replacement, and any associated regulatory costs) shall be allocated as follows:
23	
24	> \(a\) To the extent that the recall or field alert arises from the failure of Pinnacle (or any Subcontractor) to comply with cGMP, the Specifications, the Marketing Authorisations, Applicable Law, or this Quality Agreement, or from the negligence or willful misconduct of Pinnacle, Pinnacle shall bear one hundred percent (100%) of the recall costs, regardless of whether such failure is characterized as negligent, grossly negligent, or willful.
25	>
26	> \(b\) To the extent that the recall or field alert arises from causes attributable to Ceritas (including defects in API or other Ceritas-Furnished Materials, or in the Specifications provided by Ceritas), Ceritas shall bear the recall costs. In the event of shared causation, recall costs shall be allocated in proportion to each Party\'s relative contribution to the root cause, as determined by a documented root-cause investigation.
27	>
28	> \(c\) For purposes of this Section 10.2, \"recall costs\" include, without limitation: logistics and transportation costs for Product retrieval and destruction; customer and distributor notification costs; the cost of replacement Product; Regulatory Authority communication and submission costs; third-party warehousing and quarantine costs; and Ceritas\'s internal costs reasonably incurred in managing the recall, including dedicated personnel time and external consultant fees.
29	
30	For the avoidance of doubt, the allocation of costs under this Section 10.2 is without prejudice to any indemnification rights or obligations of the Parties under the MSA, and the Parties reserve all rights and remedies available to them under the MSA (including Section 11.3(d) of the MSA) and applicable law with respect to liability for product recalls and field alerts. No limitation or exclusion of liability shall apply to recall costs for which Pinnacle is responsible under this Section 10.2.
31	
32	**10.3 Cooperation.**
33	
34	Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other Party in the planning, coordination, and execution of any product recall or field alert. Such cooperation shall include, without limitation:
35	
36	> \(a\) providing all information, data, and documentation reasonably requested by the other Party or by any Regulatory Authority in connection with the recall or field alert;
37	>
38	> \(b\) making personnel available for consultation, meetings, and communications with Regulatory Authorities;
39	>
40	> \(c\) assisting with the identification and tracing of affected Batches, distribution channels, and inventory; and
41	>
42	> \(d\) taking such other actions as may be reasonably necessary to protect patient safety and to comply with applicable regulatory requirements.
43	
44	**[SECTION 11 --- SUBCONTRACTING]{.underline}**
45	
46	**11.1** **Prior Written Consent;** **Approved Subcontractors.**
47	
48	Pinnacle shall not subcontract any manufacturing, testing, packaging, storage, or other cGMP activity relating to the Product (whether to an Affiliate of Pinnacle or to a third party) without the prior written consent of Ceritas, consistent with Section 2.3 of the MSA. A laboratory listed in Annex E may be used for the scope of services identified in Annex E only after it has been audited and qualified by Ceritas and Ceritas has confirmed its approval in writing (as recorded in Annex E), and only to the extent that the laboratory is registered as a testing site in the applicable Marketing Authorisations. The laboratories proposed by Pinnacle for inclusion in Annex E are:
49	
50	> \(a\) Rheintal Analytik AG (Switzerland);
51	>
52	> \(b\) Solara Testing Services Ltd. (United Kingdom); and
53	>
54	> \(c\) QCBio Laboratories, Inc. (Maryland, United States).
55	
56	Pinnacle shall ensure that each approved subcontractor laboratory is and remains qualified to perform the testing activities delegated to it, including compliance with applicable cGMP requirements, applicable regulatory registrations, and Pinnacle\'s quality standards. Pinnacle shall maintain a written quality agreement with each approved Subcontractor and shall provide Ceritas with a copy of each such quality agreement for review and approval before the Subcontractor commences work on the Product, and shall make such modifications as Ceritas reasonably requires to ensure consistency with this Quality Agreement. Annex E shall be reviewed and reaffirmed by the Parties at least annually, and Ceritas may remove any Subcontractor from Annex E by written notice based on audit findings, performance data, or changes in risk profile.
57	
58	**11.2 New Subcontractors.**
59	
60	In the event that Pinnacle proposes to engage a subcontractor for testing or other cGMP activities that is not listed in Annex E (or that is listed in Annex E but not yet approved by Ceritas), Pinnacle shall obtain Ceritas\'s prior written consent before engaging such subcontractor and before transferring any Product, samples, data, or Product-related materials to it. Pinnacle\'s request for consent shall be submitted at least ninety (90) calendar days before the proposed engagement and shall include the identity and location of the new subcontractor, a description of the scope of activities to be subcontracted, and confirmation that Pinnacle has evaluated and qualified the subcontractor in accordance with Pinnacle\'s supplier qualification procedures.
61	
62	Pinnacle shall be solely responsible for the qualification, oversight, and monitoring of all subcontractors engaged under this Section 11.2, including ensuring that each new subcontractor complies with applicable cGMP requirements and Pinnacle\'s quality standards. No new subcontractor shall commence work on the Product unless and until it has been audited and qualified by Ceritas, Ceritas has provided its written consent, and any required regulatory submission (including any NDA supplement or EU variation adding the subcontractor as a testing or manufacturing site) has been approved or has become effective.
63	
64	Annex E shall be updated to reflect any new Subcontractor approved by Ceritas, and the Parties shall cooperate to update Annex E by written amendment to this Quality Agreement.
65	
66	**11.3 Pinnacle Remains Responsible.**
67	
68	Notwithstanding any subcontracting arrangement, Pinnacle shall remain fully responsible to Ceritas for the quality, accuracy, and compliance of all work performed by any subcontractor in connection with the Product. The subcontracting of any activity shall not relieve Pinnacle of any of its obligations under this Quality Agreement or the MSA. Pinnacle shall be solely responsible for the selection, qualification, monitoring, and oversight of all subcontractors and shall ensure that subcontractor performance meets the requirements of this Quality Agreement and applicable cGMP requirements.
69	
70	**11.4 Ceritas Audit Rights over Subcontractors.**
71	
72	Pinnacle shall include in each agreement with a Subcontractor a provision granting Ceritas and its designees the right to audit the Subcontractor\'s facilities, quality systems, and GMP documentation relating to the Product on the same terms as Ceritas\'s audit rights over Pinnacle under Section 9, and Pinnacle shall facilitate any such audit.
73	
74	**[SECTION 12 --- DATA INTEGRITY AND RECORDS]{.underline}**
75	
76	**12.1 Data Integrity.**
77	
78	Pinnacle shall maintain all electronic records and electronic signatures used in connection with the manufacture, testing, packaging, labeling, storage, and release of the Product in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures) and EU GMP Annex 11 (Computerised Systems). Pinnacle\'s compliance program shall address the requirements of 21 CFR Part 11 with respect to system validation, audit trails, system access controls, authority checks, record copying and retention, and electronic signature controls.
79	
80	Pinnacle shall implement and maintain appropriate controls to ensure the integrity, accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability of all data and records generated in connection with the manufacture and testing of the Product, including both electronic and paper-based records. All data shall be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, and accurate, as well as complete, consistent, enduring, and available (\"ALCOA+\"), in accordance with the Data Integrity Requirements.
81	
82	Pinnacle shall maintain a comprehensive data-integrity program consistent with the Data Integrity Requirements, including the FDA Guidance for Industry, Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers (December 2018) and the MHRA \'GXP\' Data Integrity Guidance and Definitions (March 2018). The program shall address, at a minimum: (a) organizational and cultural controls, including assignment of data-integrity responsibilities, management commitment, training, and a culture that encourages reporting of data-integrity issues without retaliation; (b) procedural controls, including written procedures for data generation, processing, review, and reporting, for audit-trail review, and for the identification, investigation, and resolution of data-integrity incidents; and (c) technical controls, including system-level access controls, audit-trail functionality, electronic-signature compliance, data backup and recovery, and validation of computerized systems used to generate, process, or store GMP data. Compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 alone shall not satisfy this Section 12.1.
83	
84	Any data-integrity incident affecting data relating to the Product shall be treated as a Critical Deviation for purposes of notification under Section 6.1 unless Ceritas agrees otherwise in writing. Pinnacle shall provide Ceritas QA with an annual self-assessment report on the maturity and effectiveness of its data-integrity program no later than sixty (60) calendar days after the close of each calendar year, including (i) a summary of data-integrity audits and assessments conducted during the year, (ii) a summary of data-integrity incidents identified and their resolution, (iii) the status of any open remediation activities, and (iv) management\'s overall assessment of the program\'s maturity.
85	
86	**12.2 Documentation.**
87	
88	Pinnacle shall maintain all manufacturing, testing, packaging, labeling, and quality records related to the Product in accordance with cGMP requirements and Pinnacle\'s internal document management standard operating procedures. Such records shall include, without limitation, batch production records, batch packaging records, laboratory records and raw data, equipment calibration and qualification records, environmental monitoring records, deviation and CAPA records, change-control records, training records, and validation records.
89	
90	All documentation shall be prepared, reviewed, and approved in accordance with Pinnacle\'s document management SOPs, and shall be maintained in a manner that ensures document security, traceability, and retrieval capability throughout the required retention period.
91	
92	**12.3 Records Retention.**
93	
94	GMP Records related to the Product shall be retained by Pinnacle for the longer of:
95	
96	> \(a\) ten (10) years from the date of Batch release; or
97	>
98	> \(b\) the period required by applicable law, regulation, or regulatory guidance.
99	
100	Upon the expiration of the applicable retention period, Pinnacle may destroy GMP Records in accordance with its internal records management procedures, provided that Pinnacle has given Ceritas at least sixty (60) days\' prior written notice and an opportunity to request transfer or copies of any records scheduled for destruction. Ceritas shall bear the cost of any such transfer or copying.
101	
102	During the retention period, Pinnacle shall maintain the records in a manner that permits timely retrieval and review, and shall make such records available to Ceritas upon reasonable request and during audits conducted pursuant to Section 9.
103	
104	Upon expiration or termination of this Quality Agreement, Pinnacle shall, at Ceritas\'s election, either (a) continue to retain all GMP Records for the remainder of the applicable retention period in accordance with this Section 12.3, or (b) transfer such GMP Records (or certified true copies) to Ceritas or its designee in a format acceptable to Ceritas.
105	
106	**[SECTION 13 --- STABILITY PROGRAM]{.underline}**
107	
108	**13.1 Scope.**
109	
110	Pinnacle shall perform ongoing stability testing on the Product as part of the commercial stability program, in accordance with applicable cGMP requirements, 21 CFR 211.166, ICH Q1A(R2) (Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products), ICH Q1E (Evaluation for Stability Data), and the terms of the relevant NDA and EU Marketing Authorisation. The stability program shall encompass both the 25 mg and 100 mg strengths of Velorantib Tablets and shall be designed to confirm that the Product remains within its approved shelf-life Specifications throughout its designated storage period and through expiry.
111	
112	Stability samples shall be stored under the conditions and at the intervals specified in the applicable stability protocols. Pinnacle shall maintain the stability storage chambers used for the Product in a qualified and calibrated state, with continuous temperature and humidity monitoring.
113	
114	**13.2 Protocols and Reporting.**
115	
116	All stability testing shall be performed in accordance with stability protocols approved in writing by Ceritas. Ceritas shall have approval authority over all stability protocols, including the selection of Batches for stability, testing intervals, storage conditions, and test methods. Pinnacle shall provide technical input into the development of stability protocols, which shall be consistent with the commitments made in the NDA and the EU Marketing Authorisation and with applicable regulatory requirements. No stability protocol may be amended without Ceritas\'s prior written approval.
117	
118	Pinnacle shall report stability results to Ceritas within five (5) business days of completion of each time-point analysis. Each such report shall include the individual test results for each test at each time point for each Batch on stability, and not only summary statistics or trend charts. Pinnacle shall also provide quarterly stability summary reports as a supplement to (and not in substitution for) such time-point reports. Each quarterly stability summary shall include, at a minimum, identification of the Batches on stability, the time points tested during the reporting period, the test results obtained, and an indication of any out-of-trend or out-of-specification results observed.
119	
120	In the event that any stability test result falls outside the approved Specifications or exhibits an out-of-trend or out-of-specification finding, Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation of such result (confirmation occurring upon completion of the laboratory\'s initial assessment that the result is not attributable to laboratory error) and shall initiate an investigation in accordance with Sections 6.2 and 6.4 of this Quality Agreement.
121	
122	**[SECTION 14 --- LIABILITY AND FORCE MAJEURE]{.underline}**
123	
124	**14.1 Limitation of Liability.**
125	
126	The limitations and exclusions of liability applicable to the Parties are set forth exclusively in Article 11 of the MSA, which shall govern. Consistent with Section 11.3 of the MSA, no limitation or cap on liability shall apply to Losses arising from (a) any failure to comply with cGMP, the Specifications, the Marketing Authorisations, or this Quality Agreement (including the costs of recalls, field alerts, market withdrawals, and remediation activities); (b) regulatory non-compliance; (c) infringement or misappropriation of Intellectual Property; or (d) breach of confidentiality obligations.
127	
128	Notwithstanding any exclusion of consequential, indirect, incidental, special, or punitive damages under the MSA, the following shall remain recoverable: (a) the costs of product recalls and field alerts, including all recall costs described in Section 10.2; (b) regulatory fines, penalties, and assessments; (c) third-party product-liability claims and associated defense costs; and (d) lost profits directly attributable to a quality failure of Pinnacle that results in an interruption of supply of the Product.
129	
130	**14.2 Indemnification.**
131	
132	The indemnification rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses arising out of or in connection with the manufacture, testing, packaging, storage, release, and distribution of the Product are set forth in Article 10 of the MSA, which provisions are incorporated herein by reference. The allocation of quality responsibilities under this Quality Agreement may be used to establish which Party\'s acts or omissions caused a Loss, but nothing in this Quality Agreement shall limit, reduce, or condition either Party\'s indemnification obligations under Article 10 of the MSA.
133	
134	**14.3 Force Majeure.**
135	
136	Subject to Section 14.3 of the MSA and this Section 14.3, Pinnacle shall be excused from performance of its manufacturing and supply obligations to the extent that such performance is prevented by a Force Majeure Event, as defined in the MSA. A Force Majeure Event shall not excuse, suspend, or delay Pinnacle\'s quality and regulatory obligations under this Quality Agreement, including without limitation its obligations relating to (a) deviation, OOS, and OOT notification and investigation (Section 6); (b) batch-record maintenance, records retention, and data integrity (Section 12); (c) regulatory inspection notification and cooperation (Section 9.3); (d) product-safety notifications, recall cooperation, and Field Alert Report support (Section 10); (e) Complaint investigation (Section 17 and Annex D); and (f) the protection, quarantine, and proper disposition of any Product or materials that may have been compromised by the Force Majeure Event.
137	
138	Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event that affects or is expected to affect Pinnacle\'s ability to perform its obligations under this Quality Agreement, including a description of the event, the anticipated duration, and the obligations affected. Pinnacle shall activate its business-continuity plan within twenty-four (24) hours of the occurrence of the Force Majeure Event, shall provide Ceritas with written status updates at least every forty-eight (48) hours during the Force Majeure Event (addressing the impact on manufacturing, testing, and storage operations, the status of business-continuity plan activation, estimated timelines for resumption of normal operations, and any Product-quality risks identified), and shall take all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact of the Force Majeure Event on its performance and to resume full performance of its obligations as promptly as practicable following the cessation of the Force Majeure Event.
139	
140	Pinnacle shall maintain a documented business-continuity plan and disaster-recovery plan covering the Product and the manufacturing, testing, and storage operations performed under this Quality Agreement, addressing at a minimum alternative manufacturing capacity, raw-material and component stockpiling, critical personnel backup, information-technology disaster recovery, and communication protocols. Pinnacle shall review and update such plans at least annually and shall provide copies to Ceritas upon request. If a Force Majeure Event continues for ninety (90) or more consecutive calendar days, Ceritas may terminate this Quality Agreement together with the MSA in accordance with Section 14.4 of the MSA.
141	
142	**[SECTION 15 --- TERM, TERMINATION, AND SURVIVAL]{.underline}**
143	
144	**15.1 Term.**
145	
146	This Quality Agreement shall become effective as of the date on which it is executed by both Parties (the \"Effective Date\") and shall remain in effect for so long as the MSA remains in effect, including any Renewal Term (as defined in the MSA) and any Transition Period under Section 13.6 of the MSA, and shall terminate automatically upon the final termination or expiration of all obligations under the MSA, consistent with Section 13.7 of the MSA, subject to Section 15.3 (the \"Term\"). Any renewal of this Quality Agreement shall occur only upon, and on the same terms as, renewal of the MSA.
147	
148	This Quality Agreement shall continue to apply to any Product manufactured, tested, packaged, stored, or shipped by Pinnacle after the termination or expiration of the MSA, including during any Transition Period.
149	
150	**15.2 Termination.**
151	
152	This Quality Agreement may not be terminated separately from the MSA. A material breach of this Quality Agreement shall constitute a material breach of the MSA for purposes of Section 13.3 of the MSA, and any termination of the MSA shall terminate this Quality Agreement in accordance with Section 15.1. The Parties shall amend this Quality Agreement, rather than terminate it, to the extent required to reflect changes in Applicable Law or regulatory requirements.
153	
154	**15.3 Survival.**
155	
156	Upon the expiration or termination of this Quality Agreement for any reason, the following provisions shall survive and continue in full force and effect:
157	
158	> \(a\) The obligations set forth in Section 6 (with respect to open investigations and CAPAs), Section 9.3 (Regulatory Inspections), Section 10 (Product Recall and Field Alerts), Section 12 (Data Integrity and Records, including records retention under Section 12.3 and data-integrity program maintenance for retained records), and Section 17 and Annex D (Complaint Handling), together with all obligations relating to Product manufactured, tested, or released during the Term, shall survive for a period of ten (10) years following the date of expiration or termination, or for such longer period as is required under Section 12.3 or Applicable Law.
159	>
160	> \(b\) The definitions set forth in Section 2 shall survive to the extent necessary to interpret the surviving provisions.
161	>
162	> \(c\) The confidentiality obligations applicable to information exchanged under this Quality Agreement shall survive for a period of ten (10) years following the date of expiration or termination (and, with respect to trade secrets, for so long as such information retains its trade-secret status).
163	>
164	> \(d\) The provisions of Section 14 (Liability and Force Majeure), Section 16.1 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution), and Section 16.4 (Severability) shall survive in accordance with their terms.
165	
166	All other obligations of the Parties under this Quality Agreement shall cease upon expiration or termination, subject to the completion of any Batch that is in process at the time of expiration or termination, which shall be completed, tested, released, and shipped in accordance with this Quality Agreement and the MSA.
167	
168	**[SECTION 16 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
169	
170	**16.1 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution.**
171	
172	This Quality Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, United States of America, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction, consistent with Section 15.1 of the MSA. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods shall not apply.
173	
174	Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Quality Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, shall be resolved exclusively in accordance with the dispute-resolution procedures set forth in Article 15 of the MSA (including executive-level negotiation and final and binding arbitration administered by the International Chamber of Commerce and seated in New York, New York, conducted in English before three (3) arbitrators), which are incorporated herein by reference.
175	
176	Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction to protect its rights under this Quality Agreement, including but not limited to the protection of confidential information.
177	
178	**16.2 Amendments.**
179	
180	No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Quality Agreement shall be valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, amendments to the Annexes of this Quality Agreement (including updates to Annexes A through F) shall require written agreement of both Parties, except as otherwise expressly provided herein (including updates by a Party to its own contact information in Annex A).
181	
182	**16.3 Notices.**
183	
184	All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Quality Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered personally, when sent by internationally recognized overnight courier service (with tracking confirmation), or when sent by email (with confirmation of receipt), addressed to the quality contacts and legal contacts set forth in Annex A (with a copy of any notice of breach, termination, or dispute to the addresses for notices set forth in Section 16.1 of the MSA), or to such other addresses as a Party may designate by written notice to the other Party.
185	
186	**16.4 Severability.**
187	
188	If any provision of this Quality Agreement, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court or arbitral tribunal of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Quality Agreement or the application of such provision to other persons or circumstances. The remaining provisions of this Quality Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, and the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the original intent of the Parties.
189	
190	**16.5 Counterparts.**
191	
192	This Quality Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by email (in PDF format) or other electronic transmission shall be equally as effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
193	
194	**16.6 Entire Agreement.**
195	
196	This Quality Agreement, together with the MSA and its Exhibits, constitutes the entire understanding and agreement between the Parties with respect to quality matters relating to the Product and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, negotiations, discussions, representations, warranties, and understandings, whether oral or written, relating to the subject matter hereof. No terms or conditions of any purchase order, acknowledgment, invoice, or other business form shall modify or supplement this Quality Agreement, and any such terms or conditions are expressly rejected.
197

199	
200	**17.1 Responsibilities.**
201	
202	Ceritas (on its own behalf and on behalf of Ceritas Ireland) shall be responsible for the receipt and triage of Complaints from the market, for determining whether any Complaint requires regulatory reporting, and for all communications with complainants and Regulatory Authorities regarding Complaints. Pinnacle shall be responsible for investigating all Complaints relating to the manufacture, testing, packaging, labeling, storage, or release of the Product, in accordance with this Section 17, Annex D, 21 CFR 211.198, and Chapter 8 of the EU GMP Guidelines.
203	
204	**17.2 Complaints Received by Pinnacle.**
205	
206	Pinnacle shall forward to Ceritas any Complaint received directly by Pinnacle from any source (including a customer, distributor, healthcare professional, or patient) within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt, and shall not respond substantively to the complainant without Ceritas\'s prior written consent.
207	
208	**17.3 Investigation Timelines.**
209	
210	Pinnacle shall initiate an investigation of each Complaint within three (3) business days of receipt of the Complaint (if received directly by Pinnacle) or of notification from Ceritas (if forwarded by Ceritas). An investigation is \"initiated\" when Pinnacle has opened an investigation record, assigned an investigator, and commenced the collection of relevant data, Batch records, and retained samples. Pinnacle shall provide preliminary findings to Ceritas within ten (10) business days of initiation, including (a) a summary of the Complaint, (b) a description of the investigation activities conducted to date, (c) any preliminary root-cause hypotheses, and (d) an assessment of whether the Complaint may warrant a Field Alert Report, recall, or other regulatory notification. Pinnacle shall deliver a final investigation report within thirty (30) business days of initiation unless Ceritas QA grants an extension in writing; any extension request shall describe the reason for the delay, the status of the investigation, and a proposed revised completion date.
211	
212	**17.4 Scope of Investigations; Escalation.**
213	
214	Ceritas shall have the authority to direct the scope and depth of any Complaint investigation, including by requiring additional testing, expanded Batch reviews, extended investigations, or the engagement of external experts. Pinnacle shall notify Ceritas within twenty-four (24) hours of identifying that a Complaint may involve a risk to patient safety, may trigger a Field Alert Report or other regulatory reporting obligation, or may indicate a need for a recall or other market action.

408	**Critical:** any change that requires prior approval by a Regulatory Authority (e.g., a Prior Approval Supplement or Type II variation) or that has a high potential to affect the identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency of the Product. Examples: change of manufacturing site or Subcontractor; change in the manufacturing process or batch size outside approved ranges; change to Specifications or Approved Test Methods; change of API, excipient, or primary packaging component supplier. Requirement: complete change-notification package at least ninety (90) calendar days before implementation; prior written Ceritas approval; regulatory approval before implementation or release.
409	
410	**Major:** any change with a moderate potential to affect Product quality or that requires a regulatory notification (e.g., a CBE-30 or CBE-0 supplement, an annual-report change, or a Type IA/IB variation). Examples: replacement of process or analytical equipment (including like-for-like replacements of equipment in direct contact with the Product or used for release testing); changes to cleaning procedures, HVAC, water systems, or environmental monitoring programs; changes to GMP computerized systems; changes to secondary packaging components. Requirement: complete change-notification package at least ninety (90) calendar days before implementation; prior written Ceritas approval.
411	
412	**Minor:** any change with no potential to affect Product quality and no regulatory reporting requirement. Examples: editorial SOP revisions; replacement of non-product-contact parts with identical parts; administrative changes. Requirement: management through Pinnacle\'s change-control system; listing in the monthly quality summary report; records available to Ceritas upon request.

# 2. Bottom Line

Pinnacle's draft cannot be executed in its current form. It is a CDMO-favorable template that falls below Ceritas's Mandatory Position on almost every core quality control and, in at least eleven places, contradicts terms Pinnacle already accepted in the executed MSA. The redline returns the draft to the Playbook positions. The memorandum below explains each change, how it is scored, and how to negotiate it.

- **Authority allocation is inverted.** Pinnacle's QP holds final EU disposition and Ceritas has no override (§7.1(a)). Changes are notify-and-comment on 30 days' notice (§5.2). CAPA approval sits solely with Pinnacle (§6.3). Recall decisions are joint, giving Pinnacle a veto (§10.1). Ceritas is barred from inspections (§9.3). Subcontractors can be used without Ceritas consent or audit (§11). Each of these is a Mandatory Position, and most are named examples of Critical deviations in Rubric §4.2.1.

- **Event-driven visibility is missing.** Critical deviations are notified 72 hours after classification, Major deviations only monthly, and Minor deviations never (§6.1). There are no root-cause timelines (§6.2) and no OOS/OOT provisions outside stability. Stability data is reported quarterly (§13.2), and inspections are notified within 5 business days (§9.3).
